  - Resolution: Fixed.  `_dash_json_str` reads its `0' by value through `_dash_json_str_args`, which escapes with `_json_escape` (every control character, and the backtick, dollar sign and apostrophe as `, $ and '); `_dash_json_get_str` decodes every JSON escape, \uXXXX included, in one pass.  Certified by test/test_json_escaping.cscript JSE-22, JSE-27, JSE-28, JSE-29, JSE-35 and JSE-37 (each failing at f7b28a2); registered under graph_text_options, text_plot_options, by_option and build_options.

- [x] Title: A KPI's if was read back cut at its first double quote, so its variables were not exported or dash build failed
  - File Names and Line Numbers: dash.ado `_dash_prepare_spec` (`local _kifx = "${dash_kpi_<name>__if}"`, line 4269 at ad13a0f)
  - Description: Measured 23sep2026 at ad13a0f.  The KPI's qualifier was read back through an expression in plain quotes, which ended at its first double quote: for `dash kpi mean(price) if make != "AMC" & rep78 == 3` rep78 was not exported, and both modes showed 6165.26 with a "filter skipped" warning where Stata's summarize gives 6429.23; with the literal "AMC Concord", dash build stopped with r(198) "invalid 'Concord'".
  - Suggested fix: Read the global whole, by copy.
  - Resolution: Fixed: `: copy global` and a length test.  Both modes show Stata's value (6429.23 and 6509.59).  Certified by test/test_json_escaping.cscript JSE-25, JSE-26 and JSE-32 (each failing at f7b28a2); registered under kpi.

- [x] Title: The qualifier reader ignored ~ and Unicode variable names, so `if ~foreign` and an if on a Unicode-named variable exported no variable
  - File Names and Line Numbers: dash_parse.mata `_dash_extract_qual_vars` (the operator list and the name pattern ^[a-zA-Z_][a-zA-Z0-9_]*$)
  - Description: Measured 23sep2026 at f7b28a2.  The list of operators the reader blanked held ~= but not ~, Stata's logical not, and its name pattern was ASCII-only, so `if ~foreign` (Stata: 52 rows) and an if on a variable named with an e-acute (Stata: 22) named no variable to export, and both modes drew all 74 cars.
  - Suggested fix: Split on every ASCII byte a Stata name cannot hold, keep every byte of 128 or more, which is part of a UTF-8 letter, and pass over tokens that start with a digit; the callers confirm that each name exists.
  - Resolution: Fixed in the reader: the Unicode-named qualifier now draws Stata's 22 rows in both modes, and `if ~foreign` exports foreign.  The renderer still refuses `~x` and `!x` on a numeric column (pandas cannot invert a float), so that qualifier is still skipped with a warning and draws 74 rows: recorded for a separate fix.  Certified by test/test_json_escaping.cscript JSE-30 and JSE-31 (each failing at f7b28a2).

- [x] Title: lcolor(), lwidth() and lalpha() restyled the markers' outlines, where twoway's line options never touch a marker
  - File Names and Line Numbers: dash_render.py `GlyphMapper._apply_marker_opts` (the lcolor, lwidth and lalpha blocks at 4347, 4362 and 4426 at ad13a0f), `map_pccapsym` (its own filter of those options)
  - Description: Measured 23sep2026 at 9f48cf7 and again at ad13a0f from twoway's SVG export (StataNow 19.5, console binary).  On scatter, connected, dot, dropline, rscatter, rcapsym, rconnected, pcscatter, pccapsym and scatteri, twoway draws every marker the same with lcolor(red), lcolor(red%50) or lwidth(vthick) as without them; only mlcolor() and mlwidth() change a marker's outline (lalpha() is not a twoway option at all).  dash's marker applier took the outline colour, width and opacity from those line options on every marker type but pccapsym, which filtered them out itself -- so lcolor(red) on a connected plot drew red-rimmed markers.
  - Suggested fix: Read a marker's outline from mlcolor() and mlwidth() only; keep naming an unknown lcolor() or lwidth() style, as twoway notes one even on a plot with no line.
  - Resolution: Fixed, in both modes: `_apply_marker_opts` reads the outline from mlcolor()/mlwidth() and malpha() alone, still resolves lcolor() and lwidth() so that an unknown name is noted once, and applies nothing from them; `_apply_line_opts` styles the lines as before, and pccapsym's own filter is gone.  Certified by test/test_marker_label_parity.py (failing at ad13a0f) and test_twoway_option_parity.py.

- [x] Title: mlabel() drew labels on plot types twoway leaves unlabelled, labelled the wrong ends of range plots, and none on types twoway labels
  - File Names and Line Numbers: dash_render.py GlyphMapper `map_line` (also tsline), `map_area`, `map_spike`, `map_rarea`, `map_rbar`, `map_rspike`, `map_rcap`, `map_rline` (also tsrline), `map_rconnected`, `map_rcapsym`, `map_rscatter`, `map_pcscatter`, `map_pcarrow`, `map_pcbarrow`; dash.ado `_dash_fold_bw` and the new `_dash_fold_mlab`; dash.sthlp Marker Label Options
  - Description: Measured 23sep2026 at ad13a0f against twoway's SVG export, ten observations per type.  twoway labels each point of scatter, connected, bar, dot and dropline; both ends of rcapsym, rconnected and rscatter (twenty labels); the first point, (y1, x1), of pcscatter, pccapsym, pcarrow and pcbarrow; and draws no label, without a note, on line, spike, area, rarea, rbar, rspike, rcap, rline, tsline and tsrline; mspline and mband refuse mlabel() ("too many variables specified", r(103)); histogram and function never read it, so mlabel(nosuchvar) is rc 0 there.  dash labelled all ten of the unlabelled types (the range ones at their top end), labelled rcapsym's top end only and each rconnected end twice, drew no label on rscatter, pcscatter, pcarrow or pcbarrow, accepted mlabel() on mspline and mband, and refused mlabel(nosuchvar) on histogram and function.  The help's list of the types mlabel() works on was wrong accordingly.
  - Suggested fix: Draw the labels where twoway draws them and nowhere else, refuse mlabel() on mspline and mband, and drop it unread on histogram and function.
  - Resolution: Fixed in both modes: the ten unlabelled types draw none; rcapsym and rscatter label both ends and rconnected each end once; pcscatter, pcarrow and pcbarrow label the first point; `_dash_fold_mlab` refuses mlabel() on mspline and mband with r(103) and drops it on histogram and function before the value rules; dash.sthlp's Marker Label Options says where labels are drawn and what they say.  Certified by test/test_marker_label_parity.py (146 tests, 145 failing at ad13a0f) and test/test_twoway_option_parity.cscript TP-08 to TP-12 (failing at ad13a0f), with mode-parity corpus entries; registered under text_plot_options.

- [x] Title: mlabel() of a value-labelled variable drew its codes, and a missing value as "NaN"
  - File Names and Line Numbers: dash_render.py `GlyphMapper._apply_mlabel_opts` (the label text, 4890 at ad13a0f) and `_mlabformat_column`; the new `_mlabel_value_labels`, `_mlabel_column_kind`, `_mlabel_missing`, `_mlabel_number_text` and `_mlabel_value_text`
  - Description: Measured 23sep2026 at ad13a0f.  twoway labels a value-labelled variable's points with its value labels (Domestic and Foreign for sysuse auto's foreign), an unlabelled value of it with its number as Stata writes a number into a macro (2 under %9.2f is "2", 0.5 is ".5", a %td value its day number), and a missing value with "."; .a draws its label.  dash drew the codes, 0 and 1, and a missing value as "NaN", or as nothing under a display format.  jsonio writes every missing value as null and keys value labels by the variable's name.
  - Suggested fix: Write the text twoway writes: the value label, else the number as Stata writes it, else ".".
  - Resolution: Fixed in both modes: the label text is derived once per source into a column named by the variable alone (so a served filter redraw keeps the column the LabelSet reads), value labels are looked up by label-set name and then by variable name, an unlabelled value is written as Stata's %18.0g writes it, and a missing value is "." in every format.  Certified by test/test_marker_label_parity.py, whose adversarial cases (a label keyed by another spelling of the code, markup in a value label, a huge label set, a long number) are registered under data_content.

- [x] Title: mlabangle(400) was accepted on pccapsym, where twoway refuses it
  - File Names and Line Numbers: dash.ado `_dash_option_rules` (the mlabangle rule's type list, 1369 at ad13a0f)
  - Description: Measured 23sep2026: twoway refuses a marker-label angle outside -360..360 with "textangle must be between -360.000 and 360.000", r(198), on every type that draws marker labels, pccapsym among them; the rule's type list left pccapsym out, so dash accepted it.
  - Suggested fix: Add pccapsym to the rule's type list.
  - Resolution: Fixed.  pcarrow and pcbarrow stay off the list on purpose: twoway prints the message there and returns rc 0, drawing the arrows without their labels.  Certified by test/test_twoway_option_parity.cscript TP-04 (failing at ad13a0f).

- [x] Title: `dash serve' aborts with r(7102) on every launch: the renderer refuses the extension-less app path dash.ado hands it
  - File Names and Line Numbers: dash.ado `_dash_serve' (`tempfile serve_app_path', handed to `--output' with no suffix, 4938-4952 at 4ede074); dash_render.py `_validate_output_path' (21269-21316, `expected = ".py" if mode == "server"'), called from `main' (21354); the check came in with 7ddbc08 (WP-08, TR-08.8)
  - Description: Measured 23sep2026 at 4ede074 with the console binary (sysuse auto, `dash scatter mpg weight, name(g1)', then `dash build, filter(foreign, type(dropdown)) ... nobrowser'): `dash serve, port(5487) timeout(1) nobrowser' printed "dash serve: starting Bokeh Server on port 5487" and then a Python traceback ending "ValueError: dash_render: --output must end in .py for mode 'server' (got '.../St71750.000003')", r(7102); nothing listened on the port. dash.ado passes the bare tempfile name on purpose -- its comment says the app runs as `python <path>', which needs no suffix, and a suffixed name leaked files -- and 7ddbc08 then made `main' require `.py' in server mode, so every launch aborts, the bare `dash serve' included. Nothing ran the real launch: test_serve_launch.cscript stops at the empty-registry check, test_serve_browser.cscript launches a stub renderer, and the Python tests run the generated app directly (GAPS.md C1, C2).
  - Suggested fix: Make the two sides agree -- let `main' accept the launch path's app file whatever its suffix when `--launch' is given (keeping the segment, leading-hyphen and control-character checks), or give dash.ado a registered `.py' tempfile it erases itself -- and first add a certification case that runs `dash serve, port(N) timeout(1) nobrowser' against the real renderer and waits for its exit.
  - Resolution: Fixed 23sep2026 (WP-23), recorded below; the first text of this Resolution is the historical "Not fixed" note. Not fixed. Still open (found 23sep2026 by WP-23 while measuring ROADMAP.md AC-03.1) because the fix is in dash.ado and dash_render.py, outside that documentation change, and CLAUDE.md rule 8 wants its failing test first.  Fixed 23sep2026 by WP-23: on the --launch route the renderer accepts a .py name, or a name no file holds yet, so it can never overwrite an existing file that is not a .py; `dash build, server` still needs .py, and the `..`, leading-dash and control-character checks hold on every route.  The app file stays a registered Stata tempfile, erased on success, on error and after Ctrl+C (measured: SIGINT to Stata's process group stopped the server, dash serve returned rc 0 within 0.7 s and the tempfiles were gone).  Certified by test/test_help_claims_4.py `TestTheOutputPathRule` and `TestTheRealHandoffServes` (the renderer run exactly as `_dash_serve` runs it: /health answered in 1.6 s, SIGINT stopped it at 2.0 s) and test/test_help_claims_4.cscript HC4-19 to HC4-21 (a real `dash serve, timeout(1)`: /health answered 200 while it blocked, rc 0 after 61 s, no copy of the app left); HC4-19 failed at 4ede074.

- [x] Title: A served by() panel title ignores the by() variable's display format
  - File Names and Line Numbers: dash_render.py, the app template's facet driver (`_panels.append((_dash_facet_label(by_vars, _key, val_label_names, val_labels), ...' at 20451 at 4ede074), against `DashRenderer._facet_label' (16065-16081), which also passes the numeric formats, the date variables and a date formatter
  - Description: Measured 23sep2026 at 4ede074 with dash's classes (a scatter of mpg on weight, by(rep), rep holding 3, 4 and 5 as floats): with no format, or %8.0g, both modes title the panels 3.0, 4.0 and 5.0 (the "3.0" entry above); with `formats: {rep: %9.0f}' the saved page titles them 3, 4 and 5 and the served app 3.0, 4.0 and 5.0. The served call passes the value labels only, so a variable's display format -- and a date's -- never reaches a served panel title, although the app carries the formats (`_NUM_FORMATS', WP-10). The parity corpus's by() entries use foreign, which has value labels, so no comparison sees it.
  - Suggested fix: Pass the app's numeric formats (and, once the served app handles dates, the date formatter) to `_dash_facet_label' as the saved renderer does, and add a by() entry on a formatted numeric variable to test/test_mode_parity.py's corpus, written first.
  - Resolution: Fixed 23sep2026 (WP-23), recorded below; the first text of this Resolution is the historical "Not fixed" note. Not fixed. Still open (found 23sep2026 by WP-23 while measuring the "3.0" entry above) because the fix is in dash_render.py, outside that documentation change, and CLAUDE.md rule 8 wants its failing test first.  Fixed 23sep2026 by WP-23, by another route than the one suggested: twoway titles an unlabelled by() value with its number whatever the display format (measured, test/test_help_claims_5.cscript HC5-07), so neither mode reads the format now and both title 3, 4 and 5.  Certified by test/test_help_claims_5.py `TestThePanelTitles::test_a_display_format_plays_no_part` (both modes).

- [x] Title: A refused weighted command left its weight in s(), so the next dash command, written with no weight, was weighted by it
  - File Names and Line Numbers: dash.ado `_dash_process_segment` (the varpart dispatch, about line 2440 at 4ede074) and the varpart parsers `_dash_parse_varpart_std`, `_1v`, `_3v` and `_4v` (1102-1165 at 4ede074), which set s(_weight) and s(_wexp) only when a weight is given
  - Description: Found by WP-23's run of every help example and measured 23sep2026 at 4ede074.  s() is not cleared when an sclass program starts, and the segment's `sreturn clear` came after the weight checks, so a command refused in between -- lowess or histogram refusing the weight, a weight expression, a non-integer or negative fweight, tsline with no time variable -- left its weight behind, and dash clear does not reach s().  After `dash lowess mpg weight [aw=price]` (r(101)), `dash lfit mpg weight, name(g1)` registered an lfit weighted by price; after `[aw=price+1]` was refused, every later weighted type was refused with that expression's message; and a later scatter's note named `[aweight]` -- the help's own example sequence at dash.sthlp 1526 and 1538 showed it.
  - Suggested fix: Clear s() before the varpart dispatch.
  - Resolution: Fixed: `sreturn clear` before the dispatch.  Certified by test/test_statistical_options.cscript SO-93 to SO-96 (each a refused weighted command, then the same kind of command with no weight; all failing at 4ede074) and test/test_help_examples.cscript, which runs the help's examples in one session as a user would.

- [x] Title: A third t(), b(), l() or r() after t1title() and t2title() was dropped in silence at graph level
  - File Names and Line Numbers: dash.ado `_dash_parse_graph_opts` (at 4ede074: `T() B() L() R()` declared at 567-568, and the t/b/l/r fold at 582-585 and again at 606-609)
  - Description: Measured 23sep2026 by WP-23.  `dash (scatter mpg weight), t1title(A) t2title(B) t(C)` printed "ignoring unsupported option(s): t1title() t2title()" and never named t(); the same options at plot level, in the paren form and after || named it.  Stata's syntax binds a spelling to the first declaration that admits it and is still empty, and T1title() and T2title() admit t before T() does, so the explicit T() was reached only by a third spelling on one side -- and the fold then discarded that value.
  - Suggested fix: Remove `T() B() L() R()` and the fold; T1title() to R1title() take t() to r() directly.
  - Resolution: Fixed, with the duplicated generator NOTE comment and the fold copies (GAPS M4).  Certified by test/test_alias_semantics.cscript AS-06b (failing at 4ede074) and test/test_abbreviations.py `test_no_declaration_is_shadowed_by_an_earlier_one`, `test_no_fold_is_repeated_in_a_parser` and `test_every_fold_reads_an_option_its_parser_declares`.

- [x] Title: An unknown size() or color() inside title(), xtitle() or ytitle() replaced the scheme's style with a hard-coded one
  - File Names and Line Numbers: dash_render.py `_dash_figure_title` (14259-14273 at 4ede074), `_dash_style_axis_titles` (14276-14291), `_textbox_size` and `_textbox_color` (1573-1594)
  - Description: Measured 23sep2026 by WP-23, in both modes.  The note said the unknown style was ignored, but the renderer then drew 16px or 13px and #000000: `title(T)` draws the scheme's 14pt, while `title(T, color(bogus))` under s1rcolor drew black text on a black background.
  - Suggested fix: Resolve with a default of None and set the property only when the value resolves.

- [x] Title: The console binary on a Mac opened dashboards with xdg-open, which macOS does not have
  - File Names and Line Numbers: dash.ado `_dash_render_immediate` (3727-3729 at 4ede074) and `_dash_build` (4779-4781)
  - Description: Measured 23sep2026 by WP-23.  Console Stata on a Mac reports c(os) "Unix" (c(machine_type) "Mac (Apple Silicon)"), so dash chose xdg-open: "/bin/bash: xdg-open: command not found", no window, and in the one-line form no line saying where the file was written.
  - Suggested fix: Use open when c(os) is MacOSX or c(machine_type) begins "Mac".

Certified by test/test_help_claims_2.cscript HC2-30b and HC2-34f, which run the opener against stub open and xdg-open scripts put first on the PATH (HC2-29 refuses to run unless both resolve to the stubs).  A console run on a Mac now really opens a window unless `$dash_nobrowser`, nobrowser or nodraw says not to, so every batch run keeps setting `$dash_nobrowser` (test/test_cscript_hygiene.py enforces it for the cert scripts).

- [x] Title: A filter() label holding ";", "||" or the word "exclude(" stopped dash build or was refused
  - File Names and Line Numbers: dash.ado `_dash_prepare_spec` (the exclude scan at 4245-4287 and the `_filt_work` loop at 4391-4434 at 4ede074); dash_parse.mata's new filter reader (`_dash_filter_split`, `_dash_filter_items`, `_dash_filter_refusal`, `_dash_filter_setvars`)
  - Description: Measured 23sep2026 by WP-23.  The joined filter groups were split at every "||" and ";", and every "exclude(" was taken for the sub-option: a label holding ";" or "||" stopped dash build with r(132), or r(111) for label("Origin; or not"); label(A;B) was refused as naming a variable "B)"; label("exclude(nosuch) me") was refused as an exclude().  The help said a label may be anything but a semicolon, and that repeated filter() options are joined with a semicolon.
  - Suggested fix: Split only outside quotes and parentheses, read exclude() only as a group's own sub-option, and do both in Mata, by value.
  - Resolution: Fixed; the help now says a label may hold any character and that the groups are joined with ||.  Certified by test/test_help_claims_3.cscript HC3-03 to HC3-09, HC3-11, HC3-19 and HC3-20 (HC3-03 to HC3-09 failing at 4ede074).

- [x] Title: The renderer split filter text the same way and read an apostrophe as a quote, so a label was lost or an exclude() silently dropped, in both modes

  - Description: Measured 23sep2026 by WP-23.  `label(Bob's cars) exclude(g2)` built with rc 0 in both modes, titled the widget "Bob's cars) exclude(g2" and dropped the exclude() without a word; a compound-quoted label kept its quote characters; and `type(range),exclude(g1)` built no widget.

- [x] Title: filter() with an abbreviated variable built no widget
  - File Names and Line Numbers: dash.ado `_dash_prepare_spec` (the filter group's variable)
  - Description: Measured 23sep2026 by WP-23: `filter(fore)` built with rc 0 and no widget ("the variable is not in the data"), because `confirm variable` accepted the abbreviation and handed it to the renderer, which looks up the full name jsonio writes.

- [x] Title: xtick() and ytick() replaced the axis labels when given alone, and were dropped beside xlabel()
  - File Names and Line Numbers: dash_render.py `_dash_apply_axis_options` (12941-12961 at 4ede074, `raw = xlabel or xtick`); test/test_axis_options.py `test_xtick_is_honoured` (213-216 at 4ede074), which asserted the defect
  - Description: Measured 23sep2026 by WP-23, from twoway's SVG and in both dash modes.  twoway draws xtick() positions as unlabelled marks at full tick length and keeps xlabel()'s labels, or the default ones.  dash drew labelled ticks at the xtick() positions in place of the default labels when xtick() was given alone, dropped the marks beside xlabel() -- the ordinary way to write it -- and drew nothing beside xlabel(none).  GAPS F4 and ROADMAP TR-23.1 had recorded it as fixed by WP-14/15; the help said xtick() was honoured.
  - Suggested fix: Carry the marks as minor ticks styled like the major ticks: FixedTicker(minor_ticks=...) for a fixed label set, otherwise a CustomJSTicker wrapping the axis's own ticker, with constant code and the positions passed as data; name every xtick() sub-option in the note.
  - Resolution: Fixed; two parts of WP-23 found it and fixed it independently, and one implementation was kept: `_dash_apply_tick_option`, which makes the axis's ticker a CustomJSTicker whose major, labelled ticks are the old ticker's and whose minor ticks are the xtick() positions (a numlist or a(b)c, #N, or minmax), styled as major ticks, with constant code and the positions passed as data; a categorical axis is left alone; `grid` draws grid lines at the marks, as twoway draws them (measured: 56 more line segments with `xtick(2500 3500, grid)`); another sub-option is named; and it applies to the figure's own axes, never a yaxis(2) axis.  Registered in the served app's copied helpers.  Certified by test/test_help_claims_8.py `TestXtickDrawsMarksWithoutLabels`, `TestTheTickMarkCodeCarriesNoUserText` and `TestXtickSubOptionsAreNamed` and test/test_help_claims_7.py `TestTicksWithoutLabels` (failing at 4ede074), with test_axis_options.py's `test_xtick_is_honoured` rewritten to twoway's rule.

  - File Names and Line Numbers: dash.ado `_dash_kpi` (3812, 3828-3858 and 3998 at 4ede074); dash_parse.mata (the statistic reader, 434) and the new `_dash_kpi_pctile`
  - Description: Measured 23sep2026 at 4ede074: `dash kpi p97.5(price), name(k1) title("P")` stopped with "dash kpi: syntax is stat(varname), e.g. mean(mpg).", r(198), and p100 with "percentile must be between 1 and 99", while the help said p10, p90 and p97.5 are all accepted and both renderers computed fractional percentiles. - [x] Title: A command giving name() twice was accepted where twoway refuses it, so a second name() could replace a registered graph or register a name twoway never would
  - File Names and Line Numbers: dash.ado at 68327a8: `_dash_process_segment` (the plot parser's call at 2965, whose catch-all kept a second name() of the same list, and the c_local of the graph options at 3016, by which a later segment's name() overwrote an earlier one), `_dash_plot` (the after-comma parse at 3280 and its restore at 3366, by which the after-comma name() overwrote a group's), `_dash_report_ignored` (which then named the second as "name()"); the new `_dash_refuse_second_name` and dash_parse.mata `_dash_has_name_opt`
  - Description: Measured 24sep2026 at 68327a8 with the console binary, sysuse auto.  twoway refuses any command that gives name() twice -- in another plot group, after a paren command's comma, in another || segment or twice in one option list, written name() or nam(), naming the same graph or two -- with "option name() not allowed", r(198); only when its first name() names a graph it already holds without replace does it say "graph g1 already exists", r(110), first, and when the first says replace it drops the old graph before refusing.  dash took one of the two -- the last group's, the after-comma one over a group's, the first of one list -- named the other "ignoring unsupported option(s): name()", and went on.  With g1 registered, `dash (scatter price weight, name(g1)) (line price weight, name(g1, replace))`, the after-comma form, `name(g1, replace) name(g1)` in one list and the || form each replaced g1 with rc 0; with nothing registered, every such command registered a graph, and `dash (scatter price weight, name(g1)) (line price weight, name(g2))` registered g2 alone.  dash kpi already refused a second name(): its syntax declares no catch-all.
  - Suggested fix: Refuse a second name() in twoway's words before anything is registered: in one option list, by the name() -syntax- leaves to the catch-all; across the plot groups, || segments and the after-comma options, by counting the lists that gave one.
  - Resolution: Fixed.  `_dash_has_name_opt` (dash_parse.mata) finds a name() spelled name or nam among an option list's top-level option names, quotes and parentheses honoured, so text such as title("name(x)") and an option spelled NAME() do not count; `_dash_process_segment` and `_dash_plot` refuse one left in a list's catch-all, `_dash_plot` counts the lists that gave name() and refuses at the second, and `_dash_refuse_second_name` prints "option name() not allowed" and exits 198 before anything is registered or replaced -- unlike twoway, which drops a graph its first name() replaces before it refuses.  Four hundred options in one list are past what Stata's own -syntax- reads, and it refuses them first with r(1003), "too many options", in twoway and dash alike (a hundred are refused r(198) by both).  dash.sthlp's Differences item 2 says so.  Certified by test/test_registry_collision.cscript REG-37 (every form with g1 registered), REG-38 (two names, nothing registered), REG-39 (one name() wherever written, and text or NAME() not a second), REG-40 (a KPI card) and REG-41 (a hundred in one list, sixty groups, and four hundred); REG-37, REG-38 and REG-41 failed at 68327a8, and REG-33, whose three commands were refused only because the name() dash read held no replace, is restated as the second-name() refusal it now is and failed at 68327a8 too.  Registered under name_option.

- [x] Title: `dash build` refused a dashboard of immediate graphs alone, and the one-line form refused one with no data in memory, where twoway draws both
  - File Names and Line Numbers: dash.ado at a17c552: `_dash_prepare_spec` (the refusal at 4758, before the jsonio export at 4788), `_dash_render_immediate` (the check at 3900-3903 that admitted a spec when any one plot was scatteri, pci, pcarrowi or function, the one-observation placeholder at 3904-3916, the refusal at 3918); dash_render.py at a17c552: the per-plot qualifier in the saved render loop (17561) and in the served app (21296, 21492); the new dash.ado `_dash_empty_data` and dash_parse.mata `_dash_spec_types_in`
  - Description: Measured 24sep2026 at a17c552 with the console binary.  After `dash scatteri 1 2 3 4, name(a1)`, `dash build, saving(f.html) replace` said "dash build: no variables identified across registered graphs.", r(198), and after `dash pci 0 0 1 1, name(a2)` so did `dash build, saving(f.py) server replace`.  With no data in memory the one-line `dash scatteri 1 2 3 4, saving(f.html)` said "dash: no variables identified in plot specification.", r(198).  twoway draws scatteri, pci, pcarrowi and function alone, with data in memory or none (rc 0).  The one-line route drew them only by exporting one observation of the first variable in memory, a placeholder no layer read; and it admitted a spec when any one plot was of that family, so a spec holding a scatteri beside a line with no variables was rendered and died in Python, "failed to build figure", r(7102).
  - Suggested fix: When no variable is needed and every graph is scatteri, pci, pcarrowi and function alone, write the data file directly -- jsonio's layout with no variable and no observation -- on both routes; keep the refusal for any other graph that names no variable.
  - Resolution: Fixed.  `_dash_prepare_spec` and `_dash_render_immediate` export no variable when every graph's plots are of the literal family (`_dash_spec_types_in`, which matches each "type" of a spec whole, in linear time) and write the data file with `_dash_empty_data`; jsonio is required only when there is a variable to export; the placeholder is gone; a graph of any other type that names no variable -- one dash no longer registers, but the registry is ordinary globals -- is refused on both routes as before.  twoway ignores if and in on scatteri, pci and function (their sersets hold every point whatever the qualifier), so both render modes now skip a literal layer's own qualifier: with no data the saved page said it "could not be applied" and the served app that its if_expr filter was skipped.  dash.sthlp's Plot types section says a graph of these types needs no data.  Certified by test/test_parser.cscript P1A-72 (built saved and served, with data in memory and with none; the one-line form with none; the exported file's text) and P1A-74 (the refusals, the r(7102) spec among them), both failing at a17c552, and P1A-75 (the helpers), and by test/test_immediate_dashboards.py `TestADashboardOfImmediateGraphsAloneIsDrawn` and `TestTheDataFileIsTheOneDashAdoWrites`, both modes.  Registered under plot_varlist_and_type.

- [x] Title: An immediate plot whose every point is missing was reported as drawing nothing from the observations, in a graph named '?'
  - File Names and Line Numbers: dash_render.py at a17c552: `_dash_report_empty_layer` (16219), its call in the saved render loop (17678, which named a graph with no name '?') and in the served app (21553, which named it ''); the new `_dash_note_empty_layer`
  - Description: Measured 24sep2026 at a17c552, sysuse auto.  `dash scatteri . . . ., saving(f.html)` drew nothing, as twoway does, and said "dash: graph '?' plot 1 (scatteri) drew nothing from 1 observations." -- the observation the one-line route's placeholder, '?' the saved page's name for a graph with none; `dash pci . . . .` and `dash pcarrowi . . . .` said the same.  Registered beside `dash scatter mpg weight, name(b5)` and built, it said "graph 'b4' plot 1 (scatteri) drew nothing from 74 observations.".  twoway draws nothing and says nothing (rc 0): an immediate plot draws from its own values, not from the observations.  The served app named a graph with no name ''.
  - Suggested fix: One rule, run by both modes: never report a scatteri, pci or pcarrowi layer; report a function layer drawn empty -- its expression was refused -- whatever the data, with no count of observations it never read; report any other layer when the graph's data has rows; name a graph with no name by the layer's place alone.
  - Resolution: Fixed.  `_dash_note_empty_layer` is that rule, and both the saved render loop and the served app call it; `_dash_report_empty_layer` words it, "dash: plot 1 (scatter) drew nothing from 74 observations." for a graph with no name, and "dash: graph 'g1' plot 2 (function) drew nothing." for a function.  A function expression dash refuses is still reported, now with no data in memory as well.  Certified by test/test_parser.cscript P1A-73 and test/test_immediate_dashboards.py `TestAnImmediateLayerMissingEverywhereSaysNothing`, `TestALayerThatDrewNothingIsNamedByWhatItHas`, `TestARejectedExpressionIsStillReported` and `TestTheReportHelpers`, both modes, each failing at a17c552.

- [x] Title: A plot type with its comma glued on was an "unrecognised plot type"
  - File Names and Line Numbers: dash.ado at a17c552: `_dash_process_segment` (2518, where gettoken read the plot type up to a blank alone)
  - Description: Measured 24sep2026 at a17c552.  `dash scatteri, name(x)` said "dash: unrecognised plot type 'scatteri,'." and the Supported: list, r(198); so did `dash scatter, name(x)`, `dash pci, name(x)`, `dash (scatteri, name(x))`, `dash scatteri 1 2 || scatteri, name(x)` and every other type written with its comma glued on.  twoway reads a plot type up to a blank or a comma: `twoway scatteri 1 2,name(x)` draws, and `twoway scatteri, name(x)` is refused for the values it lacks, "'0' invalid observation number", r(198).
  - Suggested fix: Read the plot type up to a blank or a comma.

- [x] Title: A plot given nothing to draw was registered with no variables, or refused in words twoway never uses
  - File Names and Line Numbers: dash.ado at a17c552: `_dash_process_segment` (2767, where the varlist parse of scatter, line and every other type that takes a y and an x was skipped when there was no varlist), `_dash_parse_varpart_any` (1173, whose anything() was required), `_dash_render_immediate` (3918)
  - Description: Measured 24sep2026 at a17c552, sysuse auto, for twenty plot types.  `dash scatter , name(z1)` registered a graph with no variables, rc 0, and so did line, connected, area, bar, spike, lfit, qfit, lowess and tsline, by the path every type that takes a y and an x shares; the bare `dash scatter` said "dash: no variables identified in plot specification.", r(198); scatteri, pci, pcarrowi and function given nothing said "something required", r(100); `dash function y =, name(f1)` was registered with rc 0 and drawn as an empty layer, "drew nothing from 74 observations".  twoway refuses all of them, whether the comma is glued, spaced or absent, in parentheses, after || or with only an if, an in or a weight: every type that takes variables with "varlist required", r(100); scatteri, pci and pcarrowi with "'0' invalid observation number", r(198); function with "expression required", r(100), and `function y =` with "nothing found where expression expected", r(111).
  - Suggested fix: Always parse the varlist, so that -syntax- refuses nothing with twoway's "varlist required"; let the literal parser take nothing, and refuse it by type.
  - Resolution: Fixed.  `_dash_process_segment` always parses the varlist of a type that takes one, so -syntax- says "varlist required", r(100), and nothing is registered; `_dash_parse_varpart_any` takes an empty list, which `_dash_immediate` refuses as a list with no whole point, segment or arrow ("dash: scatteri needs at least one point, two numbers #y #x."), r(198), as twoway refuses it, and `_dash_process_segment` refuses a function with no expression in twoway's words, r(100) or, after `y =`, r(111).  dash.sthlp's Plot types section says so.  Certified by test/test_parser.cscript P1A-69, P1A-70 and P1A-71, each failing at a17c552.  Registered under plot_varlist_and_type and immediate_scatteri_pci_values.

- [x] Title: pci was drawn in line's colour and width and with no legend key, where twoway draws it as the immediate pcspike it is
  - File Names and Line Numbers: dash_render.py at a17c552: `GlyphMapper.map_pci_literal` (8437-8487: its colour from `default_color(color_idx, "line")`, its width `scheme.default_line_width`, no legend label)
  - Description: Measured 24sep2026 from twoway's SVG export of `twoway (scatteri 5 5) (pci 0 0 1 1)`, `twoway (scatteri 5 5) (pcspike y1 x1 y2 x2)` and `twoway (scatteri 5 5) (line y x)` under s2color, stcolor, s1mono, s2mono, s2gmanual and economist: pci is stroked exactly as pcspike -- under s2mono #A0A0A0 at 8.64 where a line is #000000, under economist #7B92A8 at 12.67 where a line is 19.01 -- and keyed in the legend beside scatteri.  dash drew pci in the p#lineplot colour (s2mono's second plot #000000, where its pcspike is #a0a0a0) at the scheme's `linewidth p` (economist's 6.0px, where its pcspike is 1.5px), and gave it no legend key, so `dash (scatteri 5 5) (pci 0 0 1 1)` drew no legend.
  - Suggested fix: Draw pci through map_pcspike, as pcarrowi is drawn through map_pcarrow.
  - Resolution: Fixed.  `map_pci_literal` builds a source from the records -- its columns named as the Segment's fields, x0 to y1 -- and draws it with `map_pcspike`, so pci takes pcspike's colour, width, legend key and line options in both modes.  dash.sthlp's Plot types section says so.  Certified by test/test_immediate_dashboards.py `TestPciIsDrawnAsPcspike`, both modes, failing at a17c552 under s2mono and economist and for the legend key.  Found on the way and left as it is: under economist twoway draws pcspike and pci at the scheme's `linewidth pother`, thick (.8, two thirds of the line's 1.2), and dash draws pcspike, and now pci, at a hard-coded 1.5px -- pcspike's own width, a defect of the paired-coordinate family's widths rather than of pci.

- [x] Title: A function missing anywhere in its range drew nothing at all, and was reported as empty
  - File Names and Line Numbers: dash_render.py at a17c552: `GlyphMapper.map_function` (the eval at 9543 and the except around it)
  - Description: Measured 24sep2026.  `twoway function y = sqrt(x), range(-1 1) n(5)` draws the curve where it is defined -- its serset holds . . 0 .70710678 1 -- and `log(x)` over the same range its right half; `function y = 1/0`, `x/0`, `10^400` and `exp(1000*x), range(1 2)` are missing everywhere, and twoway draws nothing, in silence, rc 0.  dash drew nothing for sqrt(x) and log(x) over range(-1 1), and reported each of these layers as having drawn nothing: numpy warns on a value outside a function's domain, and the warning, raised inside an eval() whose builtins are emptied, looked up __import__ there and raised KeyError, which the evaluator took for a failed expression; 1/0 and 10^400 raised ZeroDivisionError and OverflowError in Python's float arithmetic.
  - Suggested fix: Evaluate with numpy's floating-point warnings off, and read Python's ZeroDivisionError and OverflowError and numpy's inf and nan as Stata's missing value.
  - Resolution: Fixed.  `map_function` evaluates under `np.errstate(all="ignore")`, reads ZeroDivisionError and OverflowError as a layer missing everywhere, and draws every non-finite value as missing, so a function is drawn where it is defined and a function missing everywhere draws nothing without a report; an expression dash refuses to evaluate is still drawn empty and reported.  dash.sthlp's Plot types section describes it.  Certified by test/test_immediate_dashboards.py `TestAFunctionIsDrawnWhereItIsDefined` and `TestAnImmediateLayerMissingEverywhereSaysNothing::test_a_function_missing_everywhere_is_not_reported`, both modes, and test/test_parser.cscript P1A-73, each failing at a17c552.  test/test_security_surface.py and test/test_resource_limits.py pinned an empty layer for 9^9^9^9 and the other power towers; they now pin a layer whose every value is missing -- each still overflows as a float, never as an exact integer, in bounded time.

- [x] Title: A date variable whose display format held a double quote, a backtick or a dollar sign lost its format on every render, or every render of it was refused with "too few quotes"
  - File Names and Line Numbers: dash.ado at 68327a8: `_dash_formats_json` (3117; the format read with `: format' at 3128 and tested inside quotes), `_dash_date_fmts_swap` (3160; the saved formats joined as macro text at 3166) and `_dash_date_fmts_restore` (3173)
  - Description: Measured 24sep2026 at 68327a8 by WP-24's program coverage.  A display format is user text: Stata accepts %td!" and %td!` (a ! puts any character into a date picture) and %tdDD!$DD.  With a date variable formatted %td!" or %tdDD!$DD, the one-line render and `dash build' both returned rc 0 and left the variable formatted %12.0g in the user's data -- the saved list the swap handed the restore was cut at the quote, or had $DD expanded as a global, so the restore read the wrong format; with %td!` every render of the variable was refused, r(132) "too few quotes", because the backtick opened a compound quote the test never closed.  A variable named twice in the swap list also lost its format: the second swap saved the %12.0g the first had set as the original.  dash's own callers never pass a variable twice.
  - Suggested fix: Read, escape and classify the format in Mata, by value, and carry the saved formats in a form no quoting can cut.
  - Resolution: Fixed.  `_dash_formats_json` reads each format with `st_varformat()' and escapes it with `_json_escape' (which writes the backtick, the dollar and the apostrophe as \u00XX) and classifies it with a regular expression in Mata; `_dash_date_fmts_swap` saves each format as its bytes' decimal codes joined by dots, which survive any quoting, and `_dash_date_fmts_restore` rebuilds it in Mata; both take their list through `list uniq'.  Certified by test/test_program_coverage.cscript PC-01 to PC-10 (ordinary, edge and hostile formats, a Unicode variable name, and both render routes drawing a date axis and leaving the format and the data as they were); PC-03, PC-06 and PC-07 each fail with the fix reverted.  `st_varformat()' takes no abbreviation where `confirm variable' and `: format' take one, so the first version of this fix, integrated with the rest of WP-24, stopped every render of `dash scatter mpg weight if dis > 100' with r(3500) "invalid Stata variable name" -- a qualifier may abbreviate a variable, and the words of its string literals are among the names read, so `if make != "d"' did the same -- and left an abbreviated date variable %12.0g, because the restore runs under capture.  All three programs now take each variable as Stata stores it, once (`unab'), and the formats map is keyed by that name, the column the renderer reads.  Certified by PC-31, which fails with either half of that reverted.

- [x] Title: A jsonio that failed left every date variable formatted %12.0g
  - File Names and Line Numbers: dash.ado at 68327a8: `_dash_render_immediate` (the export at 3916) and `_dash_prepare_spec` (the export at 4742), each between `_dash_date_fmts_swap` and `_dash_date_fmts_restore`
  - Description: Measured 24sep2026 at 68327a8 with a stand-in jsonio that exits 459, on both routes: dash swaps each date variable's format to %12.0g so that jsonio exports the number, and restores it after the export -- but the export was not captured, so a jsonio that failed ended the program before the restore, and the user's date variables were left formatted %12.0g.
  - Suggested fix: Capture the export, restore the formats, then exit with jsonio's own code.
  - Resolution: Fixed.  Both routes run `capture noisily quietly jsonio out ...', keep its return code, restore the formats whatever it was, and then exit with it; jsonio's own message is still shown.  Certified by test/test_program_coverage.cscript PC-11 (both routes, the stand-in jsonio), which fails with either route's capture reverted.

- [x] Title: dash's Mata library check did not name _dash_path_badchar, so a library without it passed and the first saving() failed with r(3499)
  - File Names and Line Numbers: dash.ado at 68327a8: `_dash_require_mata` (203; the `_needed' list at 207-213)
  - Description: Measured 24sep2026 at 68327a8.  `_dash_require_mata` checks that every Mata function dash.ado calls is loaded, so a library that compiled half way is refused at once with the functions it lacks. The check asked for one function, `_dash_check_utf8`, and took the library for whole when it was there: with a library in memory only in part -- a copy of dash_parse.mata whose compile stopped half way, or a function defined by hand -- it passed, and the first command died in Mata: after `mata clear' and a lone `_dash_check_utf8', `dash scatter mpg weight, name(x)' said "<istmt>: 3499 _dash_split_segs() not found", naming an internal function (ROADMAP AC-07.3 held only in a fresh session). - [x] Title: inrange() with a missing bound selected no rows, in both modes
  - File Names and Line Numbers: dash_render.py at a2c7502: `_stata_if_to_pandas` (10754; its `_inrange' at 10804-10810)
  - Description: Measured 24sep2026 with StataNow 19.5 by WP-24's function audit.  Stata reads a missing bound of inrange() -- `.' or `.a' to `.z' -- as no bound: inrange(x, ., 3) is x <= 3, inrange(x, 1, .) is x >= 1 and inrange(x, ., .) every non-missing x, and a missing x is never in range.  dash wrote ((x >= a) & (x <= b)) whatever the bounds, and the rewrite of Stata's missing idioms that follows it read `x >= .' as "x is missing": inrange(x, ., 3) and inrange(x, ., .) selected no row, and a bound of .a to .z was left as invalid syntax, so the qualifier was skipped and every row drawn.  Every graph, layer and KPI `if' was affected, saved and served.
  - Suggested fix: Leave out the comparison with a missing bound, and write (x == x) when both are missing.
  - Resolution: Fixed as suggested.  A bound that is a variable holding a missing value in some rows is still compared as NaN, which excludes those rows where Stata would not bound them; dash.ado exports what the qualifier names, so that case is reachable, and is not covered here.  Certified by test/test_function_audit.py::TestQualifierFunctionsSelectStatasRows (KPI cards in both modes held to Stata's own rows), which fails 8 of its cases with the old translation.

- [x] Title: A qualifier that abbreviates a variable is skipped by the renderer, and every row is drawn
  - File Names and Line Numbers: dash_render.py at a2c7502: `_stata_if_to_pandas` and `_dash_qualified_frame` (the qualifier is evaluated against the exported columns, which carry each variable's full name)
  - Description: Measured 24sep2026 by WP-24 on a2c7502 and on the WP-24 tree alike: `sysuse auto; dash scatter mpg weight if dis > 100, saving(...)' returns rc 0 with "if_expr filter skipped -- invalid syntax", and the page draws all 74 cars where Stata's `count if displacement > 100' selects 60.  Stata reads `dis' as displacement; dash.ado exports displacement under its full name and hands the renderer the qualifier as written, so the name it asks for is not a column.
  - Suggested fix: Expand each abbreviated variable of a qualifier to its full name in dash.ado, outside the qualifier's string literals, before the qualifier is written to the spec.
  - Resolution: Fixed 24sep2026: a qualifier is stored with each variable it abbreviates written out, outside its string literals, when the graph or KPI is registered (`_dash_qual_expand', from `_dash_process_segment', `_dash_graph_qualifier' and `_dash_kpi'), as Stata read it against the data then; `set varabbrev off' is honoured, and a scalar or any other name that is no variable is left as typed.  Certified by test/test_qualifier_literals.cscript QL-22 -- `if dis > 100' and `if make != "dis" & dis > 100' draw Stata's 60 rows in both modes, on the immediate route and as a plot's and a graph's qualifier, and a KPI's `if pri > 5000' gives Stata's sum -- each of whose three sites reverted fails it; PC-31 still holds that such a command draws, with rc 0, on both routes.

- [x] Title: A function layer naming a function Stata does not have draws nothing, where twoway refuses the command
  - File Names and Line Numbers: dash_render.py at 7c28802: `GlyphMapper.map_function` (9378; its name check at 9452 raises "Unsafe name in function expression") and `_dash_report_empty_layer` (16290)
  - Description: Measured 24sep2026 by WP-24's test hardening with the console binary: `dash function y = nosuchfunction(x), range(0 10), name(c)' returns rc 0, and the build draws an empty layer with the note "dash: graph 'c' plot 1 (function) drew nothing."; `twoway function y = nosuchfunction(x), range(0 10) nodraw' refuses it, "error in expression: nosuchfunction(x)", r(133) (measured again 24sep2026 with `dash function y = nosuchfunction(x), range(0 10) name(c)' and `dash build': rc 0 both).
  - Suggested fix: Refuse at registration, as twoway does, when the expression names a function outside the whitelist -- r(133), naming the function -- keeping the draw-time check for the expression text that reaches the renderer.
  - Resolution: Fixed 24sep2026 (S3 batch), recorded below; the first text of this Resolution is the historical "Not fixed" note. Not fixed: it stays open because it is a change to what dash accepts, outside test integrity.  test/test_conformance.cscript C-03 uses this layer as the control whose empty-layer note it counts, and must be given another control when this is fixed.  **Fixed 24sep2026 (S3 batch).** `_dash_fn_refuse' (dash.ado), called from `_dash_process_segment' once a function's expression is read, refuses an expression calling a name Stata has no function for, in twoway's words, "error in expression: <expression>" (echoed through `_dash_say', at most 200 characters), and with twoway's code, r(133), before anything is registered. Each name written directly before `(' outside quotes (`_dash_fn_names', dash_parse.mata, at most 100) is put to Stata as a call with 32 arguments; only an unknown function gives r(133), and nothing is evaluated (c(rngstate) unchanged). Measured 24sep2026 with the console binary: twoway refuses nosuchfunction(x), system(x), Sin(x), x*nosuch(x) + 2, the form with no `y =' and the layer inside parentheses, all r(133), and draws normal(x), max(), inlist() and sin(), rc 0. Certified by test/test_parser.cscript P1A-77 (twoway's verdict measured again on each case; the RNG state held; SMCL echoed as typed; 5,000 unknown calls refused quickly), which fails on the unfixed tree; test/test_conformance.cscript C-03's function control is now normal(x), which twoway draws and the renderer reports as an empty layer.

- [x] Title: A compound quote nested inside another is refused, where twoway accepts it
  - File Names and Line Numbers: dash_parse.mata at 7c28802: `_dash_quote_step` (1414), which tracks a compound quote with an on/off flag, so the first closing `"' ends the outer quote
  - Description: Measured 24sep2026 by WP-24 with the console binary: `dash scatter mpg weight if make == `"say `"hi"' now"'' and `dash scatter mpg weight, title(`"a `"b"' c"')' are refused, "dash: unterminated quotation in the plot specification.", r(198); twoway accepts both, rc 0.
  - Suggested fix: Track compound-quote depth in `_dash_quote_step` instead of a flag, so each `" opens a level and each "' closes one.
  - Resolution: Fixed 24sep2026 (WP-27), recorded below; the first text of this Resolution is the historical "Not fixed" note. Not fixed: it stays open because it changes the parser every scanner shares, outside test integrity; test/test_qualifier_literals.cscript holds the literals dash reads today.  **Fixed 24sep2026 (WP-27).** `_dash_quote_step' tracks compound-quote depth instead of a flag -- each `" opens a level and each "' closes one -- so all six scanners that share it read `"a `"b"' c"' as one string. Measured 24sep2026 with the console binary: twoway accepts `if make == `"say `"hi"' now"'' and `title(`"a `"b"' c"')' (rc 0), its SVG draws a `"b"' c, it accepts 10,000 nested levels and refuses an unbalanced nesting with r(132); dash refused both with r(198). Certified by test/test_parser_integrity.cscript P1B-39..47 (every scanner, both forms through dash, a nested string holding ||, a plot command, filter( and name() that registers neither a plot nor a filter, an unbalanced nesting refused r(198) with the unterminated-quotation message, 10,000 levels stored when balanced and refused when not in 0.7 s), test/test_qualifier_literals.cscript QL-23 (the nested literal draws Stata's 23 rows on both routes and in both modes, with decoys) and test/test_json_escaping.cscript JSE-72.

- [x] Title: cert_file_has missed any needle that straddled a 32,768-character piece of a line
  - File Names and Line Numbers: test/cert_helpers.do at a2c7502: `_cert_file_has` (the fget() loop at 58)
  - Description: Measured 24sep2026 by WP-24: Mata's fget() hands back a long line in pieces of 32,768 characters, and the reader searched each piece alone, so a needle across a piece boundary was never found.  A saved page is a few lines of a megabyte and more, so every one of the 423 cert_file_has calls in 37 certification scripts could miss what it looked for -- or, for an absence check, pass on what was there.
  - Suggested fix: Read the whole file, then search it.
  - Resolution: Fixed: `_cert_file_has` reads the file whole (fread in 1 MiB pieces, joined) and cert_file_count counts in the whole text.  Certified by test/test_conformance.cscript C-00, which tests the readers themselves and fails with fget() put back.

  - File Names and Line Numbers: test/test_resource_limits.cscript at a2c7502 (RL-01 to RL-13), test/test_help_claims_1.cscript (HC1-15), test/test_help_claims_3.cscript (HC3-13), test/test_help_claims_5.cscript (HC5-03)
  - Description: Measured 24sep2026 by WP-24: Stata wraps a log line at the line size, anywhere, and a Python warning starts with the path to dash_render.py, so where a message broke depended on where the checkout lives.  From a 212-character path test_resource_limits failed at RL-01, and HC1-15, HC3-13 and HC5-03 failed from a 210-character path; from this checkout they passed.  The maintainer's report of 23sep2026, RL-06 failing from a long worktree path, is this defect -- which case fails first depends on the length: reproduced 24sep2026 from a 258-character path, a2c7502 failed at RL-01's wrapped needle "set global dash_max_filter_options", and 2df1900 passed RL-01 to RL-14 from the same path.
  - Suggested fix: Search a log's logical lines, with Stata's wrapped continuation lines re-joined.
  - Resolution: Fixed: cert_log_has (test/cert_helpers.do) re-joins wrapped lines and every log search in those scripts uses it.  Certified by test/test_conformance.cscript C-00 (its log reader, which fails with the re-join disabled); each script now passes from the path it failed from, and fails there again with the re-join disabled.

- [x] Title: A filter on a saved page leaves line, tsline, area, bar, spike and dropline layers, and a connected plot's line, as they were
  - File Names and Line Numbers: dash_render.py at 7c28802: `map_line` (5432-5505; its `sorted_source` at 5468), `map_area` (5539-5622), `map_bar` (5624-5761), `map_spike` (5763-5821), `map_dropline` (8051-8147), `map_connected` (through `map_line`); `_build_filter_widgets` (`all_graph_sources` at 19236 holds only `self.sources`); dash.sthlp "What a filter move redraws" (1175)
  - Description: Measured 24sep2026 by WP-24 at 7c28802, running the saved page's own filter callback under node: with 40 rows and a move that keeps 10, the page's scatter and dot layers go to 10, while line, tsline, area (VArea), bar (VBar), spike and dropline (Segment, and dropline's Scatter) and a connected plot's Line stay at 40, with link() and without; the served app redraws every one of them at 10.  Each of these layers draws from a copy of the columns its mapper builds, which the callback neither writes (`all_graph_sources`) nor recomputes (`agg_sources`).  dash.sthlp says the saved page "does not redraw a fitted line", implying every other layer is redrawn.
  - Suggested fix: Register each mapper-built copy with the filter callback, as computed layers are in `agg_sources`, so the script rebuilds it from the kept rows in the mapper's order (sorted by x for lines and areas), as the served app does.  A BooleanFilter view on a Line is not a fix: Bokeh rejects it (E-1024, open above).  Then parametrize test_filters.py's strict xfail over the seven types.
  - Resolution: Fixed 24sep2026 (WP-27), recorded below; the first text of this Resolution is the historical "Not fixed" note. Not fixed: it stays open because it is a change to the saved page's filter script, outside test integrity.  test/test_filters.py::TestFilterReachesTheRenderedSource::test_line_filter_updates_the_rendered_source pins the line case as a strict xfail that raises only the defect's own error, so a fix turns it into a failure to be removed with it.  **Fixed 24sep2026 (WP-27).** Every mapper that draws from a copy of the rows -- a sorted line, an area, a bar, a spike, a dropline, the range and paired-coordinate plots, a scatter without its missing rows, a layer's own labels -- carries each row's id (`__dash_row__') and draws the copy with no view; `DashRenderer._collect_derived_sources' lists the copies and `_FILTER_JS' keeps the rows of each that a move keeps, in drawn order, as `derived_sources', every column included, and recomputes a bar's or a cap's width from the kept rows (`GlyphMapper._tag_spacing'), as the served app redraws them. Certified by test/test_saved_filter_layers.py::TestEveryLayerFollowsAMove, which runs the page's own filter script under node for 23 row-drawing plot types under a dropdown, a range and a slider, with link(), by() and a layer's own if/in, and compares each figure with the saved page drawn from the kept rows (on the unfixed code 179 of the file's 250 tests fail), ::TestTheLineFollowsTheMoveAsTwowayDraws and ::TestTheSpacingTag, and by test/test_filters.py::TestFilterReachesTheRenderedSource::test_line_filter_updates_the_rendered_source, whose strict xfail is removed, now over seven types. The range and paired-coordinate plots had the same defect and are fixed the same way; rbar now draws from its own rows, so a linked selection no longer highlights it on the saved page, as in the served app (dash.sthlp updated). A variable named __proto__ lost its column on every filter move; columns are now created as the object's own properties (adversarial test in the same file).

- [x] Title: A range layer with no second y variable is reported as a plot type with no glyph mapper
  - File Names and Line Numbers: dash_render.py at 7c28802: `_dash_add_glyph` (16472-16488)
  - Description: Measured 24sep2026 by WP-24: a spec whose rscatter, rarea or rcap layer gives `yvar1' and no `yvar2' draws nothing and warns "dash: no glyph mapper for plot type 'rscatter'; nothing was drawn for that layer." -- false: the mapper exists, and the missing second y variable is the cause; the empty-layer report follows it.  Only a spec written by hand reaches this: dash.ado always writes `yvar2'.

  - Resolution: Fixed 24sep2026 (S3 batch), recorded below; the first text of this Resolution is the historical "Not fixed" note. Not fixed: it stays open because it is a change to what the renderer reports, outside test integrity, and dash.ado never writes such a spec.  **Fixed 24sep2026 (S3 batch).** For a spec that reaches the renderer with a range layer naming no second y variable, both modes now say so, in the same words -- "dash: a 'rscatter' layer takes two y variables and an x variable, and this one names no second y variable; nothing was drawn for that layer." (`_dash_note_no_second_y', called by `_dash_add_glyph' and the served range branch, the type quoted by repr()); "no glyph mapper" stays for a type that has none. Pinned by test/test_layer_reports.py::TestARangeLayerWithNoSecondY (rscatter, rarea and rcap in each mode, the same wording, a full range layer still drawn, an unknown type still "no glyph mapper", a hostile type quoted). This entry's belief that dash.ado never writes such a spec was wrong: measured 24sep2026, `dash rscatter mpg weight' reaches the renderer with the x variable empty and stops in a Python traceback, r(7102), where twoway refuses "rscatter requires 3 variables: mpg weight", r(102) -- the open entry "dash rscatter, rarea or rcap given two variables stops in a Python traceback, where twoway refuses it with r(102)".

- [x] Title: BOKEH_ALLOW_WS_ORIGIN replaced the served app's websocket origin list without a word
  - File Names and Line Numbers: dash_render.py at 7c28802: the generated launcher's `__main__` block (22507-22545) and `_dash_server_app` (22455-22505, `allow_websocket_origin=_origins` at 22500); dash.sthlp's Security section (1222-1234); bokeh 3.9 server/views/ws.py `WSHandler.check_origin` (113)
  - Description: Measured 24sep2026 by WP-24 with a running app and the handshake a browser makes: Bokeh's websocket handler uses the variable, when it is set, instead of the list the app passes it.  Set to another host, the app refused localhost and 127.0.0.1 -- the page at the address the launcher printed stayed blank -- and --allow-websocket-origin did nothing; set to `*', every origin opened a session, http://attacker.example included, so any web site the user visited while the dashboard ran could read what it draws.  Nothing was printed, and dash.sthlp's Security section never named the variable.  CLAUDE.md rule 15 asks for environment variables to be verified at start-up.
  - Suggested fix: Read the variable when the launcher starts and say what it does; refuse `*', or add the variable's origins to the app's own list instead -- a choice of policy.
  - Resolution: Fixed as far as the silence: the launcher reads the variable at start, prints that Bokeh admits its origins instead of the app's list, naming them, and warns when it holds `*' that any web site can open a session; dash.sthlp's Security section says the same.  The replacement itself is Bokeh's rule and stays the operator's choice, as WP-20 pinned it ("An operator who sets it owns the origin policy"); whether dash should refuse `*', or treat the variable's origins as additions, is left to the maintainer.  Certified by test/test_adversarial_matrix.py::TestSessionOrigin::test_bokeh_lets_the_environment_replace_it (the note names the variable and what it admits; the app without it says nothing) and ::test_a_star_in_the_environment_is_warned_of, both of which fail without the note.

- [x] Title: Any dash command holding a double quote followed by an apostrophe stopped at the entry, before anything was stored
  - File Names and Line Numbers: dash.ado at 2df1900: the `dash` entry (95 `regexm(`"`0'"', ...)', 100 `_args = substr(`"`0'"', ...)'), and the UTF-8 gates `mata: _dash_check_utf8(strtrim(`"`0'"'))' in `_dash_plot' (3398, with `_dash_split_segs' at 3401), `_dash_kpi' (4335), `_dash_prepare_spec' (4644), `_dash_build' (5204), `_dash_serve_spec' (5381) and `_dash_serve' (5473)
  - Description: Measured 24sep2026 at 2df1900 with the console binary: each site put the whole command inside compound quotes in a Stata expression or a Mata line, and a text holding "' -- one that opens with an apostrophe inside double quotes, title("'90s cars"), or a qualifier's literal "' or 1 or '" -- ended those quotes early.  A graph title or qualifier stopped with r(3000), `dash kpi mean(price), title("'90s price") name(k)' and `dash build, title("'90s cars")' with r(100) ") required", their compound-quoted forms with r(133), a KPI qualifier with r(198); nothing was registered.  twoway itself refuses the plain-quoted forms on this machine, r(109) "type mismatch", under version 16 to 19, and draws the compound-quoted ones; dash now stores the text in both forms, as the maintainer asked, and each test's comment records twoway's r(109).
  - Suggested fix: Read the command by value in Mata, st_local("0"), at the entry and at every gate.

Certified by test/test_json_escaping.cscript JSE-50 (a KPI title, plain and compound, stored and drawn as typed), JSE-53 (a dashboard title) and JSE-54 (dash serve), each failing at 2df1900; the graph cases, which also needed the plot chain's own sites (the entry below), are JSE-42..49.

- [x] Title: A plot command stopped, or stored its text cut, when a title, text option, value or qualifier held a double quote followed by an apostrophe
  - File Names and Line Numbers: dash.ado at 2df1900: `_dash_process_segment' (2557 `args', 2617, 2620, 2624, 2687, 2736, 2922), `_dash_graph_qualifier' (1258-1259), `_dash_plot' (3419, 3438, 3451, 3491-3496, 3655), `_dash_register_graph' (3915, 3936), `_dash_validate_value' (1672), `_dash_check_legend' (1494, 1498), `_dash_report_ignored' (3349), `_dash_validate_opts' (2112-2113, 2132-2133), the option parsers' emptiness tests (from 666 and from 903), the varlist parsers (1133, 1150, 1167, 1184, 1224)
  - Description: Measured 24sep2026 with the entry already read by value (and at 2df1900 in brackets): `title("'90s cars")' gave r(100) ") required" [r(3000)] and its compound form r(133); after a paren command's comma, r(109); subtitle, note, caption, a legend label and by()'s title the same.  `if make == "' or 1 or '"' gave r(198) [r(3000)].  After the plot groups, `if make != "'x"' returned rc 0 with the qualifier stored as `make !=' and the named graph's JSON stored as the word x.  `legend(label(1 "'90s") top)' let `top' through, a weight refusal echoed `[aweight=cond(make==]', and `foo("'x") bar(1)' left bar() unnamed.  Each time the text was handed on inside `"..."', where its "' ended the quote.  twoway refuses most of the plain forms (r(109), r(198), r(100)) and draws the compound ones.

- [x] Title: The renderer skipped `if !x' and `if ~x' on a numeric column, and drew every row
  - File Names and Line Numbers: dash_render.py at 2df1900: `_stata_if_to_pandas' (10877-10879, which wrote Stata's ! as pandas' ~), `_dash_qualified_frame' (16209-16218)
  - Description: Reported 23sep2026 at c0200c0 and measured 24sep2026 at 2df1900 on sysuse auto: `if !foreign' and `if ~foreign' failed in pandas ("ufunc 'invert' not supported"), so the qualifier was skipped with a warning and both modes drew 74 cars, where Stata's count selects 52.  Stata's not is defined on numbers: nonzero is true, and so is missing, so !x is true exactly where x == 0; ! binds tighter than any comparison (`!foreign == 1' is `(!foreign) == 1'), and a sign right after it (`!-x') is Stata's r(198).
  - Suggested fix: Translate a not on a numeric operand as ~(x != 0), with Stata's precedence.
  - Resolution: Fixed: `_stata_logic_to_pandas' reads the qualifier's logic in one pass by Stata's precedence and truth, and writes a number wherever a true/false value belongs as (x != 0), which is true for a missing value, as in Stata.  Certified by test/test_qualifier_logic.py `TestEachModeDrawsStatasRows' (36 not-cases in both modes), `TestAKpiSumsStatasRows', `TestAFilterMoveKeepsTheQualifier' and `TestTheTranslation', and test/test_qualifier_literals.cscript QL-16 to QL-19, each failing with the fix reverted (74 carried where Stata selects 52; a KPI 2775 where Stata sums 1378; two panels where twoway draws one).

- [x] Title: Under Bokeh 3.8, the served app admitted a websocket origin whose host only begins with an allowed one
  - File Names and Line Numbers: dash_render.py at 3130fba: the generated launcher's `_dash_server_app' (the `allow_websocket_origin=_origins' it hands Bokeh's Server, at 23123); Bokeh 3.8.0's `bokeh/server/util.py' `match_host' (166-235), which `check_allowlist' (101) calls for `bokeh/server/views/ws.py''s `check_origin' (115)
  - Description: Found 24sep2026 by running the pytest suite under Stata's own interpreter (WP-25's TR-25.2): `/opt/anaconda3/bin/python3', Python 3.13.9 with bokeh 3.8.0, the one every `dash serve' on this machine runs.  test/test_adversarial_matrix.py::TestSessionOrigin::test_a_foreign_origin_is_refused failed for `http://localhost.evil.example:<port>' and `http://127.0.0.1.nip.io:<port>': the app answered the browser's handshake 101 and ACK, a session opened, where the development interpreter's bokeh 3.9.0 refuses both, 403.  Bokeh 3.8's matcher compares only as many dot-separated labels as the allowed pattern has, so `localhost.evil.example' matches `localhost' and `127.0.0.1.nip.io' matches `127.0.0.1'; bokeh 3.9 requires the label counts to be equal.  A page served from a DNS name that begins with localhost, or from a rebinding service's name for 127.0.0.1, could open a session with the dashboard and read every observation it embeds.  The development suite never saw it: it runs bokeh 3.9.
  - Suggested fix: Check origins label for label in dash, whatever Bokeh the app runs under.
  - Resolution: Fixed: `_dash_strict_match_host' holds Bokeh 3.9's rules, and `_dash_harden_origin_check', which the launcher calls before it builds its Server, puts it in the place of Bokeh's `match_host' when Bokeh's own admits a host it must refuse -- the matcher's one caller path is the websocket origin check -- and the launcher says so; dash.sthlp's Security section says it, and that `bokeh serve app.py' keeps Bokeh's own check.  Certified by test/test_adversarial_matrix.py::TestSessionOriginUnderALenientBokeh, which runs the app with Bokeh 3.8's matcher planted in its process, so the development interpreter holds the fix too (all five fail with the launcher's call removed), and ::TestTheStrictHostMatcher; TestSessionOrigin passes under Stata's interpreter again.

  - Description: Found 24sep2026 by running the pytest suite under Stata's own interpreter (WP-25's TR-25.2), /opt/anaconda3/bin/python3 with bokeh 3.8.0: (1) the single-y page's hash differed from its baseline, and the only difference in the normalised document was the Bokeh version it records ("version":"3.8.0" for "3.9.0"), so the guard was a Bokeh version check, the thing its normaliser says it must not be; (2) the long-qualifier exhaustion case took 11.1 s against a 10 s bound, where the translation itself takes 1.3 s under Python 3.13: the time was taken inside tracemalloc, whose bookkeeping costs four times as much there as under Python 3.14; (3) the text-sink safety pins were verified only on bokeh 3.9.0, so TestBokehVersion refused 3.8.0, as it should until someone checks.

  - Description: Found 24sep2026 by running the pytest suite under Stata's own interpreter (WP-25's TR-25.2), pandas 2.3.3: test/test_dates.py::TestEpochConversion::test_calendar_formats_match_statas_iso[td] failed.  One %td value past pandas' nanosecond range (1000000, or a 31dec9999 placeholder) made `pd.to_timedelta' raise, and the handler emptied every date of the variable, warning that all of them fell outside the range.  Through Stata itself, with 02-05jan2001 and 31dec9999: "5 value(s) ... fall outside", the scatter drew nothing, the page's column held nulls, the filter was a disabled RangeSlider(0,1), the KPI card was empty, and the served download and marker labels were empty.  Under pandas 3.0.1 the period kinds (%tw %tm %tq %th %ty) raised an uncaught AssertionError at their last date, and `Timestamp.value' crashed a saved page with a filter, the served download and hover and marker-label dates.  Layers computed from a date column -- fits, histograms, areas, range layers -- were drawn in nanoseconds (pandas 2.3) or microseconds (3.0) against a millisecond axis, and a missing date at -9.2e18; pcarrow and pcbarrow crashed on a date, a bar over dates was 0.8 ms wide, dropline's mlabel(date) printed ".", the KPI script wrote a year below 1000 in three digits, and a date's sum() wrapped.  Stata's own range for every date format is 01jan0100 to 31dec9999, measured with the console binary.
  - Suggested fix: Convert each value on its own to datetime64[ms] within Stata's measured range, and read date columns in milliseconds everywhere.
  - Resolution: Fixed: `_stata_dates_to_datetime' converts element by element to datetime64[ms], identically under pandas 2.3 and 3.0, a value Stata prints as a number is NaT alone and the warning counts exactly those; `_dash_float_values' reads a date column in milliseconds for every mapper and axis helper; the consumers above are corrected; dash declares pandas 2.0, the first to store datetime64[ms].  Certified by test/test_date_range.py (182 tests, 157 of which fail at 3130fba under at least one interpreter) and test_dates.py::...[td].
