On a saved page a scatter with jitter() in a graph under link() (no by()) drew from its own copy of the rows, the jittered columns living on that copy, so a selection made in another linked graph did not show on it and one made on it reached no other graph; `_linked_scatter_view' skipped jittered layers on purpose. The served app had the same defect, `map_scatter' splitting the view's rows off into a copy, and re-jittered the kept rows after a filter move, so its points moved where the saved page keeps them. Both held with no missing value at all.
  - Suggested fix: Put the jittered coordinates on the link group's shared source as columns of the layer's own, NaN where it draws no point, drawn through the layer's view, with jitter's values unchanged.
  - Resolution: Fixed (WP-27). `GlyphMapper._linked_jitter_columns' puts a linked jittered scatter's points on the link group's source as two columns of its own (_x_jit/_y_jit, or _x_jit_2/_y_jit_2 and on, past any name already there, a user's variable included), NaN off the layer's rows, drawn through the layer's view; the values are the ones jitter() always drew (the same routine over the view's rows with both values, in order, with the same seed). `_linked_scatter_view' no longer skips jittered scatters, so the saved page's filter script rebuilds the view after a move and a layer's own if/in holds; the served app, whose shared source carries the same mark, draws it the same way and keeps the points in place through a move. Pinned by test/test_saved_filter_layers.py::TestALinkedJitteredScatter (13 tests, among them test_a_selection_in_the_linked_graph_shows_on_it, test_a_selection_on_it_shows_in_the_linked_graph, test_without_a_missing_value_it_is_linked_too, test_a_move_keeps_its_rows_where_they_were, test_a_hostile_variable_name_is_only_a_column and test_many_jittered_layers_add_two_columns_each) and ::TestALinkedJitteredScatterServed, the page's scripts run under node; a move to Foreign keeps observations 2, 6, 8 and 10, Stata's `list if foreign == 1 & !missing(mpg)' on the same ten rows (measured 24sep2026).

- [x] Title: A served filter move re-jitters a jittered scatter's kept points, where the saved page keeps them in place
  - File Names and Line Numbers: dash_render.py: the generated app's filter callback (step 3, where a redrawn layer's data is copied onto its live source); `_apply_jitter', `GlyphMapper._build_jitter_source'; now `_dash_keep_jitter'
  - Description: Found 24sep2026 by WP-27's linked-jitter work, suspected by that agent and confirmed by test. A jittered scatter draws from a copy its mapper builds, so the served app redraws it after a filter move through the mapper, from the kept rows alone; `_apply_jitter' then draws fresh noise over fewer rows with a narrower range, and every kept point moved -- observation 2 from (3391.1, 16.98) to (3358.4, 16.89) after a move to Foreign, jitter(5) jitterseed(7). The saved page keeps a move's rows of the jittered copy by row id and moves none. Stata jitters once, when it draws; a filter is dash's own.
  - Suggested fix: When a redrawn source's data is copied onto the live source, take each _x_jit/_y_jit value from the source's pre-move snapshot for the same row label.
  - Resolution: Fixed (WP-27). `_dash_keep_jitter' gives each kept row the jittered point the first draw gave it, matched by row label from the snapshot the served app takes before any move, and the filter callback applies it to every redrawn source; a row the snapshot never held keeps its fresh value. Pinned by test/test_saved_filter_layers.py::TestAnUnlinkedJitteredScatterServed::test_a_move_keeps_its_rows_where_they_were (seen failing first: all four kept points moved), with ::test_the_spec_is_unlinked as its control; the linked case is K's TestALinkedJitteredScatterServed.

- [x] Title: A saved dashboard overflows horizontally at phone width: grid columns and facet panels never narrower than about 220 px
  - File Names and Line Numbers: dash_render.py: every gridplot() grid (`_dash_layout_cell', `_dash_tab_panels', `_dash_bs_grid', `DashRenderer._assemble_layout'), the filter bar and the filterposition(left) row, and the generated app's grid, sidebar and filter bar; `_dash_kpi_card_html' and its twin in `_FILTER_JS'; now `_dash_reflow', `_DASH_MIN_COLUMN_PX', `_DASH_BS_STACK_BELOW_PX'
  - Description: Found 24sep2026 by WP-27's responsive check (TR-27.2), measured in headless Chrome through an iframe exactly 375 px wide. examples/geometry_responsive.do (layout(bs)) kept its by(foreign) facet panels side by side at 266 px each -- a page 545 px wide, one figure offscreen -- though dash.sthlp says that under layout(bs) "below 768 every item takes the whole row"; examples/full_dashboard.do (layout(3 2)) kept two 220 px columns, 440 px wide, two figures offscreen. Every gridplot() grid left its CSS columns at auto, so no column could be narrower than its figure's natural minimum, about 220 px: a 1 x 4 grid, a by(, cols(4)) facet grid and a facet inside a tab overflowed a 768 px window the same way (880 and 1228 px). The filter bar did not wrap (411 px at 375), filterposition(left) kept its 240 px sidebar beside the grid (405 px, figures 135 px), and in the served layout(bs) grid beside the sidebar the KPI cards' fixed 160 px minimum made the page 813 px wide at 768.
  - Suggested fix: Give every grid equal shrinkable columns and stack a grid of n columns into one when it is narrower than n x 240 px (a container query on the grid itself); stack the served layout(bs) GridBox below a 768 px window; wrap the filter bar; stack the sidebar row below 768 px; let a KPI card narrow below 160 px; in both modes.
  - Resolution: Fixed (WP-27). `_dash_reflow' gives each gridplot() grid cols minmax(0, 1fr) and an inline stylesheet that stacks it into one column, in reading order, when it is narrower than ncols x 240 px -- so a facet grid inside a narrow cell or tab stacks while the grid around it keeps its columns; the served layout(bs) GridBox keeps its spans down to a 768 px window and then stacks; the filter bar wraps; the filterposition(left) row stacks below 768 px; KPI cards take min-width:min(160px,100%), in the Python card and its JS rebuild alike. dash.sthlp describes the behaviour at phone width, and that the served app on a real phone lays out at desktop width, declaring no viewport. Pinned by test/test_responsive_layout.py::TestPagesFitInChrome::test_saved_page_fits (11 layout families rendered from specs, each measured in headless Chrome at 375, 768 and 1440 px: no page wider than its window, nothing offscreen or overlapping, every figure at least 200 px wide and 100 tall; without Chrome it skips, which fails a DASH_STRICT=1 run), ::TestServedDocumentsFitInChrome::test_served_document_fits (6 families), ::TestTheProbe, ::TestReflowModel, ::TestReflowAdversarial, ::TestEveryGridIsReflowed and ::TestKpiCardMayNarrow; on the unfixed code 10 of the 11 saved families and all 6 served ones failed. Measured on the Stata-built example pages after the fix: geometry_responsive is 375 px wide at 375 (figures 351 px) and full_dashboard 375 (figures 375 px), bs_responsive, bs_stacked and bs_kpi_hero unchanged, every page with nothing offscreen or overlapping at all three widths.

- [x] Title: A string value holding an unclosed compound quote, a lone backtick or apostrophe, or the closing pair stops every export inside jsonio; every strL is exported as "null"
  - File Names and Line Numbers: dash.ado: the jsonio export on the one-line route (`jsonio out' of the needed variables) and on the `_dash_prepare_spec' route (`jsonio out' of all variables); jsonio.ado lines 55 and 307-310, which expand the JSON written in compound quotes; now `_dash_write_data' and dash_render.py's `_dash_write_stata_data'
  - Description: Found 24sep2026 by WP-27's quoting work (JSE-72's decoys) and measured on 5 observations of auto with mlabel(s): jsonio's Java writes the file, but its ado then returns the JSON in a macro and expands it inside compound quotes, so a string value, value label or variable label that leaves them unbalanced stops the export whatever the qualifier -- `" or a lone backtick r(132) "too few quotes", "' or a lone apostrophe r(109); $, \, ", CR/LF, control bytes, multibyte UTF-8, `c1' and `=1+1' round-tripped. jsonio also wrote every strL as the text "null", flagged numeric, so a strL column arrived empty.
  - Suggested fix: Write the data file without jsonio, reading each value through the Stata Function Interface.
  - Resolution: Fixed (WP-27). dash.ado's `_dash_write_data' writes the data file from Stata's Python through dash_render.py's `_dash_write_stata_data', which reads every value through sfi, in jsonio's layout (missing numbers "null", every number a double, value labels keyed by variable, jsonio's codes for .a-.z labels); no value passes through a macro, the path and names reach Python through Macro.getLocal, names are checked to be Stata names before any command is built from them, a strL exports as a string, invalid UTF-8 is read through ustrfix() (U+FFFD, as jsonio wrote it) with a note naming where, a binary strL is refused r(198), and dash no longer calls jsonio. Measured in Stata: every str# and strL value, variable label and value label of test/test_string_values.cscript -- 24 adversarial values alone and together, a 1 MB strL, labels holding quotes, every storage type, missing values and dates -- reaches both the saved renderer's frame and the served app's `_load_spec_and_data()' byte for byte (SV-01..SV-04, SV-08; on the old code SV-01 fails at its first value, r(132)); invalid UTF-8 SV-06; a binary strL SV-07; a build with jsonio off the ado-path and out of memory SV-09. Also pinned by test/test_string_value_export.py::TestTheWriter, ::TestTheLabelKey, ::TestBothRenderersLoadEveryValueExactly::test_saved_and_served, ::TestThePageCarriesNoValueAsMarkup::test_a_script_end_in_a_value_stays_inside_the_json and ::TestDashAdoUsesTheWriter. A 1e5-row, 7-column export is no slower (warm 0.20-0.51 s against jsonio's 0.33-0.59 s).

- [x] Title: No byte cap on the exported data: a strL dataset makes an unbounded page
  - File Names and Line Numbers: dash.ado: `_dash_limit_table', the one-line form's and build/serve's exports; dash_render.py: `_DASH_LIMITS', the saved renderer's and `ServerAppBuilder''s loads; now `_dash_byte_cap', `_dash_text_bytes', `_dash_refuse_overbytes'
  - Description: Found 24sep2026 by WP-27, once dash's own writer exported strL values in full (jsonio had written each as "null"). $dash_max_cells counts values, not bytes: 60 observations of a 1,000,000-byte strL were 60 values, far inside the cells limit, and 60 MB of page.
  - Suggested fix: Add a bytes limit to the WP-19 table, enforced in Stata before the file is written and in the renderer for a data file that arrives another way.
  - Resolution: Fixed (WP-27). $dash_max_bytes limits the bytes of text in the string values exported, as Stata stores them, strL included: default 50,000,000, ceiling 500,000,000, a bad value refused through `_dash_limit' as the other limits refuse one. Over it both routes stop with r(134) before the file is written, in the cells cap's words ("dash: this dashboard would embed N bytes of text (in K string variables), more than the L dash embeds." and the same remedy). Nothing is read when every string variable is a str# whose width times _N fits; otherwise the lengths are summed in Mata a million observations at a time; the renderer counts only a data file larger than the limit. Measured in Stata: auto's make holds 871 bytes (the sum of strlen), refused under a limit of 870 and built under 871; 60 x 1,000,000-byte strL refused at the default and 50 admitted; a 100,000-row build is within 1% of its time before (median of 5). Pinned by test/test_adversarial.cscript P19-27..P19-30 and P19-05/18/19/20 (now eight limits), test/test_resource_limits.py::TestTheBytesOfTextAreLimited and ::TestTheTwoLanguagesAgree::test_the_help_documents_every_limit_with_its_numbers, registered in test/test_adversarial_matrix.py. **Reconciled 21oct2026 (WP-33 33-15):** `TestTheBytesOfTextAreLimited` no longer exists: the maintainer removed the bytes cap (P4-3), and test/test_resource_limits.py::TestTheBytesOfTextAreNotLimited and ::TestNoSizeCap::test_the_cap_code_is_gone pin that no cap is left.

- [x] Title: An unresolvable #include note is printed twice by one dash scatter build
  - File Names and Line Numbers: dash_render.py: `DashRenderer.__init__' and `DashRenderer._make_figure', which each parsed the scheme; `SchemeParser._include', where the note is raised; now `DashRenderer._scheme_for'
  - Description: Found 24sep2026 by the S3 batch, once an #include that resolves nowhere was noted as Stata notes it. Measured in Stata with b2inc.scheme holding `#include b2nosuch': `twoway scatter mpg weight, scheme(b2inc) nodraw' prints "(note: scheme b2nosuch not found, using s2color)" once; `dash scatter mpg weight, scheme(b2inc)' printed it twice, as did a registered graph with scheme() and then dash build, while dash build, scheme() (saved and served) printed it once. On the one-line route the graph's scheme() is also the build's, so __init__ parsed the file for the build and _make_figure again for the graph, and the catch_warnings blocks between them reset Python's duplicate suppression. S3: a note repeated.
  - Suggested fix: Parse each scheme name once per build.
  - Resolution: Fixed (S3 batch). `DashRenderer._scheme_for' keeps the renderer's parsed schemes by name, so each scheme is read once per build and each of its notes printed once; a second build notes it again; two different unresolvable includes still give two notes, and a graph scheme other than the build's is still noted. Pinned by test/test_immediate_scheme.py::TestAnIncludeNoteIsPrintedOncePerBuild (the one-line route, a build and a graph scheme, a graph scheme other than the build's, two builds, the served builder, and 50 graphs naming one scheme parsed once) and test/test_custom_scheme.cscript CS-15, which counts each note's lines in the log against twoway's -- the one-line route, a registered graph, dash build saved and served -- and failed with "found 2" on the unfixed tree.

- [x] Title: A repeated option kept its first copy and was named as unsupported, where twoway takes the last copy, merges the copies, or refuses a unique one
  - File Names and Line Numbers: dash.ado: `_dash_parse_graph_opts' and `_dash_parse_plot_opts' (-syntax-'s * catch-all), `_dash_process_segment' (the graph-option accumulator it overwrote), `_dash_plot' (the after-comma value copied over); dash_render.py: `_dash_reference_lines' (every xline()/yline() position drawn in one style); now `_dash_opts_repeats', dash_parse.mata's `_dash_rep_*', `_dash_refline_instances', `_dash_refline_draw'
  - Description: Found 24sep2026 by the S3 batch's option-parity fix. twoway reads a repeated option three ways (measured from its SVG exports, as repeated_options.sthlp says): the last copy wins for most options (`mcolor(red) mcolor(blue)' and `mc(red) mcolor(blue)' draw blue, and an earlier bad value is never read); the copies merge for titles, axis labels and ticks, legend(), xscale()/yscale(), the regions, by(), xline()/yline() and text() (`title(A) title(, color(red))' is A in red, `xlabel(2000 3000) xlabel(4000, add)' labels all three); and a unique option -- name, saving, scheme, aspectratio, xsize, ysize, nodraw, yaxis, a bare sort, kernel and bwidth on the smoothers, and others -- refuses its second copy, "option scheme() not allowed", r(198). -syntax- bound the first copy and put later ones in the catch-all, named as unsupported; `title(A) title(B)' bound the second to title2() and a second xlabel() went to xlabel2(), the second axis, in silence; a later plot group's graph option overwrote an earlier one's, so legend(label(1 ..)) in one group was lost beside legend(label(2 ..)) after the comma, with no note; and unique options given twice were accepted. Measured against twoway on the unfixed code: 31 of 33 commands stored otherwise than the command twoway draws alike (16 with a misleading note, the rest silent), and all 12 unique-option cases accepted. S1 for the silent forms.
  - Suggested fix: Rebuild the option list as twoway reads it before the parsed values are used: last copy, merged copies or a refusal, by option, and merge graph options across segments by the same rule.
  - Resolution: Fixed (S3 batch). `_dash_opts_repeats' (dash.ado) and dash_parse.mata's `_dash_rep_*' run after each parse: when a spelling repeats or one is a prefix of another, each distinct spelling (at most 100) is put to the parser alone to learn which option it is, and the list is rewritten with one copy of each -- the last, or the copies merged by twoway's rule (a later text replaces, sub-options merge keeping the last of each, suffix, prefix and add honoured, an xscale range() the union) -- a unique option given twice refused in twoway's words, r(198); the list is parsed once more, so no note names a repeat. `_dash_plot' merges graph options from plot groups, || segments and after the comma in that order and refuses a unique option given in more than one place; the renderer draws each xline()/yline() copy in its own style. twoway's ceiling of 256 options holds: 10,000 copies are r(1003) in both. Pinned by test/test_twoway_option_parity.cscript TP-14a (33 command pairs, twoway's SVGs compared in the run), TP-14b (12 refusals, sort and sort(varlist) in either order), TP-14c (the one-line route and name() then dash build), TP-14d (repeated yline() copies kept apart) and TP-14e (10,000 copies, 255 options in under 10 s, a hostile value stored as escaped text, an unbindable copy still refused), by test/test_axis_options.py::TestRepeatedReferenceLines and test/test_alias_semantics.cscript AS-06b.

- [x] Title: A function layer with a blank before a parenthesis, function y = sin (x), was drawn where twoway refuses it
  - File Names and Line Numbers: dash.ado: `_dash_fn_refuse'; dash_parse.mata: `_dash_fn_names', which saw only a name written directly before `('; now `_dash_fn_space_call'
  - Description: Found 24sep2026 by the S3 batch's function-name fix. twoway refuses "error in expression:  sin (x)", r(111), for any name the data does not have (abs, max, c, nosuch, X, _b) anywhere in the expression, r(198) for a variable of the data, x, _n, _N, _pi, a number, a string or `)' before the blanks, r(133) when only tabs separate the name and `(', and whichever error comes first (`nosuch(x) + sin (x)' r(133), `sin (x) + nosuch(x)' r(111)); it accepts sin(x), 2 * (x), x + (1), -(x), x^(2) and sin( x ). dash drew sin (x) as sin(x), rc 0. S3.
  - Suggested fix: Find an operand followed by blanks and `(' and refuse with twoway's code, asking about unknown functions only for the calls before it.
  - Resolution: Fixed (S3 batch). `_dash_fn_space_call' (dash_parse.mata) finds the first such operand outside quotes; `_dash_fn_refuse' first refuses an unknown function written before it, r(133), then the operand: r(133) for tabs only, r(111) for a name that is not a variable of the data nor x, _n, _N or _pi, r(198) otherwise, the expression echoed through `_dash_say'. Measured 24sep2026 on 35 twoway expressions and the tab and mixed cases. Pinned by test/test_parser.cscript P1A-78: 22 refused forms held to twoway's codes measured in the run, 11 accepted forms, plot-group and || forms, SMCL echoed as text, a 5,000-term expression in under 10 s, and the scanner on its own.

  - File Names and Line Numbers: dash.ado: `_dash_plot' (the replace fold beside saving(), "named in the note" otherwise)
  - Description: Found 19oct2026 by WP-32. `dash scatter mpg weight, replace', `dash (scatter mpg weight), replace', `dash scatter mpg weight, name(g) replace' and `dash scatter mpg weight, name(g) saving(f) replace' were rc 0 with "ignoring unsupported option(s): replace". The one-line form beside a saving() keeps it, as dash.sthlp documents ("saving() keeps a file that is already there": replace after the comma, as for dash build), although twoway refuses it there too; that deviation is left to the maintainer. `_dash_plot' reads every segment and the options after the comma for a saving() and a name() before any list is judged (`_dash_seg_saving', the new `_dash_seg_named') and sets the global dash__rep_ok on the one-line form with a saving(); elsewhere `_dash_tw_refuses' classes a bare replace as a word twoway does not take, so `_dash_refuse_unknown' refuses it in the list's order, "option replace not allowed", r(198), and nothing is registered or written. Pinned by test/test_option_validation.cscript U53 (failing on the unfixed code; U53-0b keeps the one-line saving() replace); test/test_path_validation.cscript PV-25, which expected the note, is flipped.

- [x] Title: A scheme's quoted values (RGB colours, %opacity) were dropped without a warning
  - File Names and Line Numbers: dash_render.py SchemeParser._parse_lines (tokens[-1] as the value)
  - Description: GAPS2 D1's measured symptom: `color background "255 0 0"' was stored under a malformed key, so the directive was lost without a warning; a scheme written with quoted RGB drew every series in its `color p' default instead, with 0 warnings; the same reader stored every shipped scheme's `label "s2 color"' line under the key `label "s2', and never skipped a `sequence' line.

- [x] Title: The saved page embeds every row of each drawn variable, including rows that if and in exclude
  - File Names and Line Numbers: dash_render.py at 7421d3d: DashRenderer._make_figure_body (25920); dash.ado at 7421d3d: _dash_write_data (4308)

Every saved source, the linked source and its views, the filter snapshot and the CSV text pass through _make_source/_dash_embed_frame; the served shared source, placeholders, widgets, brush rows and linked refresh use the same plan. Row identities are dense in both modes: the saved __dash_row__ ranks the page's rows, and the served frame is relabelled to the same ranks by _dash_page_index/_dash_relabel, so no index column carries an observation number. Every launch of the served app has a key, and nothing is served without it. _dash_token_auth is Gate A: a Bokeh AuthProvider that refuses every page, /autoload.js, /metadata and websocket request without the key with a constant 403 before any handler runs (python app.py and dash serve). _dash_session_token_ok in make_document is Gate B: it refuses every session without the key before the rate limiter and before the data is decoded; it is the only gate under bokeh serve, where a start without DASH_SERVE_TOKEN makes its own key at the first session (_dash_process_key, _dash_bokeh_serve_key). The key is _dash_new_token (secrets, 256 bits), checked by _dash_token_valid and compared by _dash_token_matches (hmac.compare_digest); a websocket's session JWT is read by _dash_ws_payload, bounded before Bokeh decodes it. dash serve hands the key to the app with --token-stdin on S08's stdin pipe, after the app text, never in argv; _dash_write_link writes the link to a 0600 link.html in the run folder, or to a fresh private folder when the run folder cannot hold 0600, or, where no folder can, writes that file with one dash: note: naming it (ratified 01oct2026); the path is printed and the key never is; where no file can be written at all, the link is printed once after a warning line while the server keeps serving (ratified 01oct2026, round 2). A start given no key makes its own (_dash_server_app before any session under python app.py; _dash_process_key and _dash_bokeh_serve_key at the first session under bokeh serve); its link is written by _dash_announce_key through _dash_private_page, 0600 in a fresh 0700 folder, and only the path is printed. _dash_open_tokenized opens the link with no key in argv, _dash_tokenized_url names 127.0.0.1, never localhost, and the redaction (_dash_redact_query, _dash_install_access_log_redaction) keeps every query string out of Tornado's logs and the launcher's forwarded output.   - Resolution: Fixed 01oct2026 (WP-29, P0.19). dash_setup inspects the linked Python in a child process (dash_setup_lib.detect_environment) and on an externally managed or pip-less Python runs no pip, printing the PEP 668 or ensurepip guidance (H7a, H7g); dash_setup, venv(path) creates or reuses, installs into and verifies a private environment and prints the python set exec line (H7b); every printed command is the resolved c(python_exec) quoted by dash_setup_lib.shell_line for POSIX shells and cmd.exe, and a managed Python gets no upgrade line (H7c, H7d, H7e, N4); a --user install is added to sys.path in the same run (H7f); pip's output is decoded as UTF-8 (N1); pip runs c(python_exec), not sys.executable (N2), from a private directory with -P, without an inherited PYTHONPATH and with PIP_BREAK_SYSTEM_PACKAGES=0 (N3, security). No renderer change; a venv-linked session builds a saved page and serves /health (scripts/release_gate_venv.do). Pinned by test/test_setup_pep668.py::TestRunChild::test_a_pip_package_in_the_working_directory_is_not_run, test/test_setup_pep668.py::TestRunChild::test_non_ascii_output_under_an_ascii_locale_is_decoded, test/test_setup_pep668.py::TestShellLine::test_the_posix_line_survives_sh, test/test_setup_pep668.py::TestValidateVenvPath::test_refusals, test/test_program_coverage.cscript PEP-01, test/test_program_coverage.cscript PEP-08, test/test_setup_honesty.cscript PEP-18; fixture test/fixtures/pip_refusals.json. Residual, deferred (WP-29): Windows quoting, Scripts\python.exe and Debian's ensurepip-less venv are tested as pure functions only; dash's own helper and in-process imports are found in the working directory first (Stata's and Python's rule). Closes GAPS2 H7 (WP-29, H7).

Sources: REM-§2-S09-lstyle, REM-§2-S09-mstyle, REM-§2-S09-areastyle, REM-S09-73-namedstyles, REM-05-04-S09-g, GAPS2-B11-a, GAPS2-B11-b, GAPS2-D6, AUDIT-29, AUDIT-30 (the p# names).

  - Resolution: Fixed 08oct2026 (WP-30, P1.14a). The named styles p1 to p15 are drawn on every plot type, as twoway draws them. pstyle(), lstyle(), clstyle(), mstyle(), mlstyle(), astyle(), alstyle(), bstyle(), blstyle() and p() are declared with twoway's abbreviations and written per series. The nine stylelists split across an expanded varlist, and p() is one name whose first copy wins (_dash_rep_cat "F"). Under p() the spec drops every style option twoway discards, the label style included. SchemeParser.style_bundle resolves p# to twoway's marker, line and area bundles from the plot index alone. GlyphMapper._style_plan applies them in twoway's factor order: each glyph takes its role's bundle once, before any explicit option (in the three appliers, and right after the glyph is built in map_area, map_rarea, map_bar, map_rbar, _histogram_quads, map_dropline, map_rcapsym, map_scatteri, map_pcarrow and map_pcbarrow), and an explicit option before the style in that order is not applied. Each type's lines take the style twoway styles them with: the connecting line on the line types, the outline on spike, range, pc and bar types. Closed by disposition under maintainer decision M12: every function layer of a graph registered in Stata is drawn from the points Stata computes with twoway's own generator (WP-29 P0.6), in the saved page and the served app, before and after a filter move, and the thirteen expressions the item names are pinned against twoway's serset; the points-free fallback, which only a spec without points reaches (one written by hand, or a registry whose points were removed or are not dash's), keeps its ten functions by design. What was left was its silence: such a layer reported only that it drew nothing. Now _stata_fn_parse's refusal carries the function or name it refused (exc.dash_refused, messages unchanged), GlyphMapper.map_function marks the empty layer with the reason (GlyphMapper._mark_needs_points, GlyphMapper._needs_points_why), stored points that cannot be read included, and _dash_note_empty_layer gives one note in both modes -- "drew nothing: it needs the points Stata computes for it when dash registers the graph, and this spec carries none; without them dash evaluates only x, _pi, numbers, + - * / ^ and the ten functions, and normalden() is not one of them" -- naming the function, the bare name (the name pi) or neither (the expression cannot be read with them), with at most 32 characters of a name echoed; the served app carries it inside GlyphMapper, and dash build, server prints it through its trial render. _dash_fn_spec_tail's note for stored points that are not dash's says they are not used and how to store Stata's, where it promised that the layer is drawn from its expression. - [x] Title: Served build on the event loop
  - File Names and Line Numbers: dash_render.py make_document (the generated app's template), the served move path
  - Description: GAPS3.md H3, the parts WP-31 section 55 left open: make_document builds on the event loop (1.6-4.6 s at 100-200k rows; no per-session memory bound, 64-150 MB per session at 200k rows by decision); library catch_warnings can swap filters; a brush made while a move waits is cleared.
  - Suggested fix: build the document off the event loop (a worker thread with a next-tick handoff), keep warnings filters per thread, and keep a brush made while a move waits.
  - Resolution: Fixed 18oct2026 (WP-32), as the maintainer ruled (DECISIONS D39), in three commits. (1) The build: python app.py (and so dash serve) serves through _DashBuildHandler, whose on_session_created -- awaited by Bokeh before the session exists, while the hook alone holds the document -- runs make_document on the process's two build threads (_dash_build_pool, _dash_build_off_loop); modify_document then has nothing left to do, a failed build is logged, and a build that never ran is made inline. Deviation from the proposed recording proxy: the document handed to the hook is already the session's and nothing else reads or writes it there, so it is built in place and nothing is replayed. A build draws with a mapper and scheme of its own (_DASH_CTX; make_document reads _dash_cur_mapper() and the new _dash_cur_scheme()), so the module's are never swapped under the loop, and a session's moves copy its own (_doc_mapper, _doc_scheme); the session limiter and the open-session cap run under one gate (_DASH_BUILD_GATE), and _STORAGE_TYPES is rewritten without being emptied. /health and a second session were answered while a first session's build was held. (2) The warning filters: a serving process (the launcher, a bokeh serve session; never loading the app, a trial or Stata's process) installs the locked class as warnings.catch_warnings once per process (_dash_lock_library_warnings), so pandas', numpy's and Bokeh's blocks are serialised with dash's own; the app's class is built on the real one kept in the holder, so a re-run app never nests. (3) The brush: a move's plan records each source's selection (_dash_sel_snapshot); when the result is drawn, a selection made since then is read by its rows' index labels before the rows are rewritten (_dash_sel_held) and selected again in the new rows (_dash_sel_restore), so a brush made while the move waited is kept on the rows the move keeps. Pinned by test/test_served_build.py::TestTheLoopAnswersWhileASessionBuilds::test_health_and_a_second_session, ::TestTheBuildOffTheLoopDrawsTheSameDocument::test_threaded_equals_inline, ::TestABrushMadeWhileAMoveWaitsIsKept::test_kept, ::TestTheSelectionHelpers, test/test_served_worker.py::TestTheWarningFilters::test_library_blocks_serialise_with_dash_own, ::test_only_a_serving_process_locks_the_library. Residual: under bokeh serve, which gives an app no session-creation hook for a script, the build still runs on the loop (BUGS.md "Under bokeh serve a session's dashboard is still drawn on the event loop"); a catch_warnings block a library binds before the lock is installed (from warnings import catch_warnings) is not serialised. Closes GAPS3 H3 (WP-32, H3).

- [x] Title: A renderer without its source file cannot write a served app
  - File Names and Line Numbers: dash_render.py _dash_source_of, ServerAppBuilder
  - Description: GAPS3.md K2, the part WP-31 section 60 left open: ServerAppBuilder copies the renderer's functions with inspect.getsource, which has no fallback; imported from a .pyc with no .py beside it (an install that kept only bytecode), `dash build, server` and `dash serve` fail with "OSError: source code not available" (test_wp31_truth.cscript U60-6 pins the refusal).
  - Suggested fix: ship the app's source text as data beside the renderer (or embed it at build), or refuse earlier in dash's words naming the missing file.
  - Resolution: Fixed 18oct2026 (WP-32), as the maintainer ruled (DECISIONS D39). Inside an app build (_DASH_STUB_SINK, set by ServerAppBuilder._generate_app_source around _generate_app_source_body), _dash_source_of writes an object inspect.getsource cannot read as a stub (_dash_stub_source): a function as name = _dash_stub_fn(key), a class as Name = _dash_stub_class(key) (its body the code object the compiled module runs for its class statement), _KERNELS as its assignment of stubs, each with a comment naming the globals its code reads so the scan for copied constants still finds them. _dash_stub_prelude writes the collected code (marshalled, compressed, base64) and the two binders, which make each function and class anew with the app's own globals, before the first stub; the app checks first that it runs under the Python that compiled the code and says so in one line when it does not. A renderer with its source writes the app as before (no stub). The app built from a .pyc-only renderer draws the same document as the one built from the source. Pinned by test/test_sourceless_renderer.py::TestASourcelessRendererWritesTheApp::test_the_app_draws_the_same_document, ::test_it_runs_only_under_the_python_that_wrote_it, ::test_a_renderer_with_its_source_writes_text, test/test_wp31_truth.cscript U60-6 (flipped: a .pyc-only renderer writes a served app). Residual: such an app runs only under the Python version that wrote it. Closes GAPS3 K2 (WP-32, K2).

- [x] Title: The scheme visual truth covers 4 of 26 schemes and renders no histogram

  - Description: GAPS3.md K3, the part WP-32 left open: test/fixtures/scheme_visual/truth.json and its eight PNGs are Stata renders of stcolor, s2color, economist and s1mono only, measured by hand (no committed generator), and no histogram is rendered.

On the four schemes the hand record held, the generated record agrees on every compared fact but economist's legend box, which the SVG draws in the graph region's own colour where the hand record called it absent (the same look); its hand-written list of disagreements is dropped, each being a fact now compared for all 26. test/test_scheme_visual_truth.py compares every fact for all 26 schemes and the histogram (GlyphMapper.map_histogram's fill, opacity, outline colour and outline width ratio); differences found: none in dash's colours, symbols, patterns, sizes, opacities or histogram bars (sttrans's 0.20 marker and bar opacity agrees); stgcolor, stgcolor_alt, stgcolor_meta and stgcolor_mv draw the histogram outline at 3.00 units, the floor of Stata's SVG writer (measured: lwidth(vvvthin) and vvthin are 3.00 units on square graphs of 1 to 16 inches, vthin 3.00 up to 2.392 inches), which is the export device's and not compared; meta's legend outline, which twoway does not draw and dash draws black, is filed as BUGS.md "meta's legend has no outline in twoway and a black one in dash". - [x] Title: meta's legend has no outline in twoway and a black one in dash
  - File Names and Line Numbers: dash_render.py SchemeParser._init_properties (legend_border_color from `color legend_line'); scripts/extract_scheme_truth.py (no legend linestyle resolution); dash-meta.scheme
  - Description: Found by WP-32's scheme visual truth (BUGS.md "The scheme visual truth covers 4 of 26 schemes and renders no histogram"). scheme-meta.scheme sets `linestyle legend none'; twoway draws the legend box's outline as a zero-opacity stroke (measured 18oct2026, StataNow 19.5: `stroke:#EAF2F3;stroke-opacity:0.00'), so no outline is seen. dash reads `color legend_line', which meta inherits black from s2color, and the translated dash-meta.scheme carries no `linestyle legend', so dash draws a black outline round the legend and the KPI cards.
  - Suggested fix: resolve the legend's outline in scripts/extract_scheme_truth.py as plotregion_line_truth resolves the plot region's (legendstyle -> `linestyle legend' -> none means no line), regenerate scheme_truth.json and the 26 dash-*.scheme files, and have SchemeParser draw no legend outline when it is none (Bokeh's Legend.border_line_color None; the KPI card's CSS border in the fill colour).
  - Resolution: Fixed 18oct2026 (WP-32), through the scheme translation pipeline. The first text of this Resolution was "Not fixed: it stays open because the fix runs through the scheme translation pipeline ..., past this package's time box". Stata's chain is legendstyle default -> boxstyle scheme legend -> `areastyle legend legend' -> areastyle-legend.style's `set linestyle scheme legend' -> `linestyle legend', which meta sets to none (scheme-meta.scheme:48), while `color legend_line' stays s2color's black (lstyle(legend) still draws it: style_truth's N|meta|lstyle|legend). scripts/extract_scheme_truth.py resolves that chain (legend_line_truth: legend_line_drawn and legend_linestyle in scheme_truth.json) and writes `linestyle legend none' into dash-meta.scheme where Stata draws no outline -- regenerated, not hand-edited; the other 25 files are unchanged. SchemeParser.legend_outline (new) is False where `linestyle legend' is none, in a shipped or a user's scheme; _dash_scheme_chrome then gives the legend no border (border_line_color None) and css_block borders the KPI card in its own fill, in both modes. Pinned by test/test_scheme_visual_truth.py::test_legend_border_is_what_stata_drew[meta] (flipped: it asserted the difference), test/test_scheme_key_readers.py::test_metas_legend_and_kpi_cards_have_no_outline, which failed on the unfixed code, and test/test_scheme_rendered_output.py's legend and KPI card colour tests (flipped for meta: no outline). test/test_scheme_fidelity.py::test_the_style_name_hops_are_identity takes `linestyle legend' beside `shadestyle plotregion' as a carried word, not a hop (flipped).

- [x] Title: The server fixture leaks a process when __enter__ fails, no AST count of the app's dispatch, hand-written scheme-key enumeration, no CSS-guard served arm, two strict xfails
  - File Names and Line Numbers: as cited
  - Description: GAPS3.md K4, re-verified at 6370ca4: Harness: the server fixture leaks a process when `__enter__` fails (test_server_serves.py:123-142); no AST count of the generated app's dispatch; scheme-key enumeration hand-written; no CSS-guard served arm; tracking-document counts unchecked; strict xfails test_natscale.py:76 and test_by_scales.py:426 (known divergences).
  - Suggested fix: WP-31 section 60 (test harness fixtures): fix the leak and add the guards.
  - Resolution: Fixed 18oct2026 (WP-31, K4), in part. _Served.__enter__ and _Launched.__enter__ (test/test_server_serves.py) wait through _wait_ready inside try/except BaseException that calls __exit__ before it re-raises, so a server or launched app that never answers (or any error while waiting) is terminated, not left running for the session (one such bokeh serve from test_data_table.py's served table test was still running a day later); both take a deadline (default 60 s). Python embedded in Stata never runs its exit handlers, so the dash_pytest_ folder test/conftest.py made when a cscript's python: block imported it stayed behind (about 140 MB a cert run); scripts/stata_batch.sh now gives each Stata run a dash_pytest_stata TMPDIR of its own and removes it when Stata ends, passing Stata's exit status on. Pinned by test/test_server_fixture.py::TestNoLeak (never-ready server, never-ready launched app, early exit, default deadline) and test/test_temp_cleanup.py::test_a_stata_run_gets_its_own_removed_python_temp. Residual (WP-31): the other guards K4 names stay open (BUGS.md "Harness guards"; GAPS3 K4 Tracked). Closes GAPS3 K4 in part (WP-31, K4).

- [x] Title: Harness guards
  - File Names and Line Numbers: test/ (the generated app's dispatch, the scheme-key list, the CSS guard, the tracking counts); test/test_natscale.py:76, test/test_by_scales.py:426
  - Description: GAPS3.md K4, the parts WP-31 section 60 left open: no AST count of the generated app's dispatch; the scheme-key enumeration is hand-written; no CSS-guard served arm; tracking-document counts unchecked; strict xfails test_natscale.py:76 and test_by_scales.py:426 (known divergences).
  - Suggested fix: count the dispatch from the app's AST, derive the scheme keys from SchemeParser, add a served arm to the CSS guard, check the tracking counts, and close or re-file the two divergences.
  - Resolution: Fixed 18oct2026 (WP-32), each guard a commit and red before it (by mutation where the tree was already right). The dispatch count: test/test_server_dispatch.py::TestTheAppHasNoDispatchOfItsOwn parses the generated app, skips every definition that is a verbatim copy of dash_render.py's, and pins every plot-type comparison the app's own code makes, whatever its spelling (test_its_own_code_tests_plot_types_only_where_pinned: the four caller-dispatched types and mband/mspline in _dash_draw_layer, the launcher's estimator line), the dispatch tables, adders and layer source as the renderer's own definitions (test_the_dispatch_is_the_renderers_own_code) and one _dash_draw_layer (test_one_layer_drawer); it replaces test_server.py's string hand count. The scheme keys: test/test_scheme_consumption.py::TestNoParsedKeyIsDiscarded::test_the_key_is_read_somewhere takes every public attribute SchemeParser._init_properties assigns (140, from its syntax tree; the hand-written list named 22), its reader also counts getattr reads whose base names a scheme by expression (axis_title_gap_px), and the six keys nothing reads are pinned unread by test_an_unread_key_is_still_unread (note_font_size by design; five filed as BUGS.md "Five scheme keys are parsed and read by nothing"). The CSS guard's served arm: TestSchemeCssActuallyApplies::test_every_selector_matches_a_class_the_served_app_emits (auto and bs) requires every class selector of the served css_block() on some served Div and the rule in the stylesheets of every Div carrying it. The tracking counts: test/test_tracking_documents.py::TestTheCountsAreTrue::test_the_wp31_closeout_counts_are_computed computes ROADMAP.md's WP-31 entry, GAPS3-row and open-entry counts from the documents at the closeout commit. The two strict xfails: test_by_scales.py e01 was a divergence -- the bystyle expansion wrote rescale, which beat noyrescale, so `style(rescale) noyrescale` rescaled y where twoway shares it (measured 18oct2026 with noxrescale, norescale and style(combine) too); _dash_bystyle_rescale_words keeps the no-word, pinned by test/test_bystyles.py::TestTheExpansion::test_a_no_word_beside_the_style_still_wins, and the xfail is flipped; test_natscale.py's three model misses are re-filed as BUGS.md "The natscale model misses three of the 264 axes twoway drew" and pinned by test/test_natscale.py::TestTheRuleAgainstStata::test_the_three_known_misses_are_still_missed. Closes GAPS3 K4 (WP-32, K4).

- [x] Title: Five scheme keys are parsed and read by nothing
  - File Names and Line Numbers: dash_render.py SchemeParser._init_properties (by_legend_ring, zyx2_ring, text_option_vertical, numticks_minor, legend_span), GlyphMapper._colorvar_key_place, _dash_added_text, _dash_apply_axis_options, _dash_apply_legend (legend(span)); test/test_scheme_consumption.py _UNREAD_KEYS
  - Description: Found by WP-32 (BUGS.md "Harness guards") when test_the_key_is_read_somewhere took its keys from every attribute _init_properties assigns instead of a hand-written list of 22: of 140 parsed keys, six have no reader in dash_render.py. One is by design (note_font_size: Stata's note() box reads `gsize small_body`, not `gsize note`). Five are keys twoway's style files read and dash parses and then ignores, so a scheme that changes them draws no differently in dash: `gridringstyle by_legend_ring` and `gridringstyle zyx2legend_ring` (bygraphstyle-*.style's legend_ring and zyx2legend_ring), `vertical_text text_option` (textboxstyle-text_option.style), `numticks_g horizontal_minor` and `vertical_minor` (ticksetstyle-minor_*.style) and `yesno legend_span` (bygraphstyle-*.style's legend_span). Every shipped scheme gives the values dash draws by default (s2color and stcolor: ring 3 and 4, middle, 0 minor ticks, no span), so only a user's scheme shows the difference.
  - Suggested fix: give each key its consumer in the shared drawing code (both modes), measured against twoway with a user scheme that changes it, and take it off _UNREAD_KEYS.
  - Resolution: Fixed 19oct2026 (WP-32): every key is read (by_legend_ring earlier; zyx2_ring, text_option_vertical and numticks_minor Fixed 18oct2026 (WP-32); legend_span, with legend(span), Fixed 19oct2026 (WP-32)), each below. Measured 18oct2026 (StataNow 19.5, SVG, a user scheme `#include s2color' plus the one key, adopath for the session only): every key changes twoway's drawing, so none is removed. (1) by_legend_ring: read. `gridringstyle by_legend_ring 0' draws `twoway (scatter mpg weight) (scatter trunk weight), by(foreign)' byte for byte as s2color with by(foreign, legend(ring(0))), and 1 as legend(ring(1)), which is ring 0's drawing; _dash_by_keys takes the scheme's ring when legend() gives none and draws ring 0 and 1 alike (pinned by test/test_by_axes_keys.py::TestTheSchemesByLegendRing::test_the_schemes_ring_is_the_default and ::test_legend_ring_still_wins). (2) zyx2_ring: read (Fixed 18oct2026 (WP-32)). Measured with the random clip-path ids masked: `gridringstyle zyx2legend_ring 0', 1 and 2 draw `twoway contour depth northing easting' and `twoway scatter mpg weight, colorvar(price)' as s2color with clegend(ring(0)), (ring(1)) and (ring(2)); ring 0 is the key inside the plot region at 3 o'clock (the plot region the graph's width), 1, 2 and s2color's 4 alike with nothing else on the side, and beside legend(pos(3)) ring 2 is drawn between the plot and the legend where 4 is outside it. dash read clegend(ring(0)) only with position() and put the key outside otherwise; GlyphMapper._colorvar_key_place takes position() else the scheme's zyx2legend_position and ring() else zyx2legend_ring, draws ring 0 inside at the clock, and tags an outside key ring=<n> and inserts it after the side's axes, edge titles, ring-tagged boxes of a ring at or inside its own and (at ring 3 or more) the series legend, so _dash_move_legend puts the ring 3 legend inside a ring 4 key and outside a ring 2 one. Pinned by test/test_scheme_key_readers.py::TestTheColourKeysRing (scatter and contour, both modes) and test/test_scheme_key_readers.py::test_the_ring_orders_the_key_beside_the_legend, which failed on the unfixed code. (3) text_option_vertical: read (Fixed 18oct2026 (WP-32)). Measured: `vertical_text text_option top', `bottom' and `baseline' draw byte for byte as text()'s alignment(top), (bottom) and (baseline), at the default size and at size(huge), the baseline 0.35 of the text size below the point at middle, 0.20 at top and bottom alike, 0.50 at baseline, two lines shifting together; dash drew every text at middle and named alignment(). _dash_added_text_opts honours alignment() (_DASH_ADDED_TEXT_HONOURED, `valign'), and _dash_added_text shifts the Label from middle's place by _DASH_ADDED_TEXT_VSHIFT (0.15 of the size up for top and bottom, 0.15 down for baseline) along the text's own up (x_offset and y_offset, which by()'s panel scaling multiplies), the scheme's text_option_vertical where alignment() is not given. Pinned by test/test_scheme_key_readers.py::TestTextVerticalAlignment, which failed on the unfixed code. (4) numticks_minor: read (Fixed 18oct2026 (WP-32)). Measured: `numticks_g horizontal_minor 4' draws byte for byte as s2color's xmlabel(#4) and `vertical_minor 3' as ymlabel(#3), and xmlabel(#2) beside the scheme's 4 draws its own; _dash_apply_axis_options gives axis 1 the scheme's count as its xmlabel()/ymlabel() rule `#N' when none is given (s2color's 0 draws none). Pinned by test/test_scheme_key_readers.py::TestTheSchemesMinorTickset, which failed on the unfixed code. A second axis keeps no scheme count (not measured). (5) legend_span: read (Fixed 19oct2026 (WP-32)). Measured 18oct2026 (ids masked): the scheme's yes draws byte for byte as s2color's legend(span), `legend_span yes' with legend(nospan) as s2color, and by() is unchanged by it (bygraphstyle's own legend_span) -- so legend(span) was the same difference, which dash took in silence (_dash_apply_legend's step 7b said a side-panel legend already spans its side; it does not). Measured 19oct2026 (stcolor and s2color, SVG of `twoway (scatter price weight) (scatter mpg weight), ylabel(, format(%15.2fc))' with legend(pos(#) [span])): span places the box along its side on the whole graph where twoway otherwise places it on the plot region -- 6 and 12 centred on the graph's width (stcolor x 2700 of 5400, the plot region's centre 3098; s2color 1980 of 3960; xsize(10) 3600), 3 and 9 on its height (y 1620 of 3240, the plot region's 1440, with title() and note() as without), 7 and 11 at the graph's left end, 4 and 8 at its bottom; 1, 2, 5 and 10 sit where they did (the plot region reaches that end); ring(0) is unchanged by span, and ring(5) spans as ring 3 does. Bokeh's side panel runs the frame's length and only BokehJS knows the frame's place in the canvas, so _dash_apply_legend's step 7c (legend(span), else the scheme's legend_span, undone by legend(nospan)) registers the legend with _dash_span, one CustomJS per figure (_DASH_SPAN_JS) on its laid-out size (inner_width, inner_height, outer_width, outer_height, which BokehJS sets after every layout: load, a resize, a move that changes the tick labels); it gives the legend the numeric location that puts its box at its place on the canvas along the side, the place across the side read back from BokehJS's own keyword placement. Both modes run it (the served copy tuples carry _dash_span, _DASH_SPAN_JS and _DASH_SPAN_KEYS); _dash_by_keys drops it from by()'s panels. Pinned by test/test_scheme_key_readers.py::TestTheLegendSpans (both modes; it failed on the unfixed code), ::test_the_span_hook_adds_replaces_and_drops, and test/test_legend_span_browser.py::TestTheLegendSpans (headless Chrome, both modes: 6, 3 and 7 o'clock at load and after the page narrows, and the place across the side kept at the default margin and bmargin(large)); legend_span is off test/test_scheme_consumption.py's _UNREAD_KEYS. Not measured: by(, legend(span)), which twoway centres on the graph (2700 against 2756 without, measured 19oct2026), is drawn as dash draws by()'s legend cell. Graded S3 (WP-32): no shipped scheme draws differently; a user scheme's legend_span, and legend(span), placed the legend on the plot region where twoway places it on the graph.

- [x] Title: A by() panel row was taller than its panels
  - File Names and Line Numbers: dash_render.py _dash_layout_cell, _dash_by_title_cell
  - Description: Found by WP-32 (BUGS.md "Without span by()'s legend was placed on its cell, not on the panels", where it was noted unfiled). twoway centres the shared y title on the panels and puts the x title right under them (measured 19oct2026, StataNow 19.5, stcolor, session-only `set scheme`, SVG of `twoway (scatter price weight) (scatter mpg weight), ylabel(, format(%15.2fc)) ytitle("Price") by(foreign, legend(pos(3)))': the y title at y 1499.34 of 3240, the centre of the panels' box 113.4 .. 2885.3; the x title at x 2251.29, the centre of 226.0 .. 4276.8). In headless Chrome at 1400 px (both modes) dash's panel row was 807 px tall for panels 560 px tall, 247 px of empty row above the x title, so the y title sat 72 px below the panels' middle. Cause: a by() panel keeps the array's proportion (aspect_ratio 0.83) and is held to _MAX_FIGURE_HEIGHT, which BokehJS writes as `max-height: min(560px, 100%)`; a grid row of auto height cannot resolve that percentage while it is sized, so the row took the proportion's height (1.2 times the panel's width) and the panel then stopped at 560 px. Below about 930 px of panel width (760 and 1000 px pages) the bound does not bind and the row fitted, but there too both axis title cells' frames were aligned with the panels' frames (BokehJS's frame_align), so the y title sat 16.6 px below the panels' middle and the x title off their centre: centred on the plot regions, not on the panels.
  - Suggested fix: give the panel its bound as a plain max-height and stop the title cells' frame alignment.
  - Resolution: Fixed 19oct2026 (WP-32). _dash_layout_cell gives each by() panel with a height bound an InlineStyleSheet `:host { max-height: <n>px !important; }`, so the row is sized by the bound and the panels fill it; _dash_by_title_cell sets frame_align False on dash_by_ytitle and dash_by_xtitle, so each title is centred on the cell's canvas, which spans the panels. In both modes, at 1400, 1000 and 760 px. Pinned by test/test_legend_span_browser.py::TestByPanelsFillTheirRow (headless Chrome, both modes, three widths: the y title on the panels' middle, the x title's row right under them and its text on their centre) and test/test_by_axes_keys.py::test_the_panels_fill_their_row (both modes), which failed on the unfixed code. The browser probe now reads a turned title's box by its angle. Graded S3.

- [x] Title: A colordiscrete key and its colours keep the build's levels after a filter move
  - File Names and Line Numbers: dash_render.py GlyphMapper._apply_colorvar (the discrete branch), _dash_by_keys; the saved page's and the served app's filter callbacks
  - Description: Found by WP-32 while measuring which levels by()'s discrete colour key holds. Measured 19oct2026 (StataNow 19.5, stcolor, session-only `set scheme`, SVG of `twoway scatter price weight if <cond>, colorvar(rep78) colordiscrete [by(foreign, clegend(on)) | by(foreign, ilegends)]'): (a) at build dash draws as twoway does -- by()'s key holds the first panel's levels (with Domestic holding rep78 1-3 and Foreign 3-5, the key reads 1-3), and each panel colours its own levels with the palette's first colours (rep78 3 is #AAFF00 in Domestic and #0000FF in Foreign), in both modes; pinned by test/test_by_axes_keys.py::test_the_discrete_key_holds_panel_ones_levels_as_twoways_does. (b) twoway levels the rows it draws: with `if rep78==3' every panel and the key hold the one level, drawn in the first colour (#0000FF); with `if rep78>=4' the levels 4 and 5 take the first two colours (#0000FF, #00FF00), with and without by(). dash's mappers, keys and legend items keep the build's levels after a filter move: in the served app, moving filter(rep78) to 3 leaves Domestic's factors 1-5 and the key's labels 1-5, so rep78 3 keeps the third colour; a graph without by() keeps its factors 1-5 the same way (served app, checked 19oct2026; the saved page was not checked).
  - Suggested fix: on each filter move, in both modes, re-level a colordiscrete layer over the rows kept -- each panel its own levels, palette's first k colours -- and rebuild by()'s key from the first panel's levels.
  - Resolution: Fixed 19oct2026 (WP-32). The first text of this Resolution was "Not fixed: it stays open because re-levelling a discrete colour key after a move means recomputing every colordiscrete mapper's factors and palette and every key's items in the saved page's filter callback and in the served app ... past this package's time box"; the maintainer ruled it be fixed. It overrides WP-29's BR-07.4 ("the key and each observation's colour are fixed at build time ... a filter move never re-ranges them") for keys of a variable's own levels. GlyphMapper._apply_colorvar leaves a relevel plan (_dash_cvar) on a layer of its own levels (colordiscrete with no cuts, a string): the build's levels in order, the palette of each count of levels as the build makes it (colorlist(), colpalette() or the colour rule's k + 1 steps), the mapper and each key it draws (its legend, one item a level, the missing entry, the plot holding the swatches); _dash_by_keys adds by()'s discrete key to the first panel's plan. After every move _dash_cvar_relevel (new; the served app, after its sources are written) and dash_cvar_relevel (new, _DASH_CVAR_RELEVEL_JS at the end of the saved page's filter callback, its plans in the callback's cvar_plans) give the mapper the build's levels the colour column still holds and their first colours, recolour each kept item's swatch, keep the missing entry while a row is missing, put the kept items in the key (reversed under colorkeysreverse) and their swatches only in the plot. Pinned by test/test_mode_parity.py's move corpus (scatter colordiscrete after a dropdown and a range move, by(foreign) colordiscrete with clegend(on) after a range move and a dropdown to rep 3: the served app against the saved renderer over the kept rows, and the saved page's own script under node against the served app) and TestTheByColourKeyAfterAMove::test_the_key_follows_the_first_panel (all three ways), which failed on the unfixed code. test/js_runner.py reads and writes back what the relevel touches (a renderer's source and glyph, a legend's items, a plot's renderers, a discrete mapper, a glyph's colours) and resolves a stand-in's own references; _shown_notes counts a legend item only while a legend on a plot holds it (a removed level's item stays in the callback's plan). Pins moved: test_served_resources.py _SAVED_DIGEST (the filter code only; masked diff, both Pythons). Graded S3.

- [ ] Title: The natscale model misses three of the 264 axes twoway drew
  - File Names and Line Numbers: dash_render.py _dash_natscale_ticks; test/test_natscale.py _KNOWN
  - Description: Re-filed by WP-32 (BUGS.md "Harness guards") from two strict xfails of test/test_natscale.py::TestTheRuleAgainstStata::test_the_axes_twoway_drew. dash's natscale model (Stata's `_natscale` is compiled) draws the ticks wherever Stata's own are not embedded: after a filter move and for a spec built without them. It agrees with 261 of the 264 axes in test/fixtures/natscale_truth.json; on auto it differs on three, re-measured 18oct2026 (StataNow 19.5, `_natscale` and `twoway scatter <var> weight, ylabel(#N)`, .Graph.yaxis1.major): price #4 (3291 to 15906) twoway draws 5000(5000)15000 where the model gives 0(5000)15000, and trunk #2 and #3 (5 to 23) twoway draws 0 and 20 (natscale's r(max) is 23 with delta 20) where the model gives 0(10)20. At build every axis a page built in Stata draws is Stata's own (WP-31 D15 for the variables' ranges; WP-34 AX-3 for every other range, asked as the page is built), so the model draws only after a filter move, and for a page rendered outside Stata; a move back to all the rows restores Stata's answers on every axis the plan carries, and a colour key keeps the model after any move.
  - Suggested fix: extend the fitted model to natscale's two quirks (a lowest tick left off above the data's minimum; an r(max) at the data's maximum with a step wider than half the range) without losing any of the 261 agreements or the 2,829 random ranges, then take the cases off _KNOWN.
  - Resolution: Not fixed: it stays open because natscale is compiled and the model is fitted to its answers; WP-31 D-45b ruled the three cases not fixable blind, and a refit that keeps the other 261 axes and the random-range floor is a model change beyond a harness guard. Pinned by test/test_natscale.py::TestTheRuleAgainstStata::test_the_three_known_misses_are_still_missed, which fails the day the model draws one of them as twoway does. Graded S3 (WP-32): three axes of 264, only after a filter move; D41 keeps them open (natscale is a compiled built-in); re-scoped by WP-34 34-09 (PD-9). Re-examined 18oct2026 under D39 (1) (WP-32): `_natscale` is still compiled and undocumented (ado/base/_/_natscale.sthlp gives only r(min), r(max), r(delta), r(n)); on the same axes it puts the lowest tick inside the data at #3 and #4 (price 5000(5000)15000) and below it at #5 (0(5000)15000), so no end rule the model can carry fits all three without the other 261 axes; a step rule tried against the fixture's 2,878 random ranges (a 1-2-5 step at or above range/(N-1)) agrees on 2,290, under the current model's 2,829. It stays open: closing it needs natscale's own algorithm or a refit across the whole fixture, not a rule for three axes. Re-examined 19oct2026 (WP-32) for an exact route first: none exists after a move. `which _natscale` says "built-in command", findfile finds no _natscale.ado or .mata and Mata no _natscale() (StataNow 19.5), and twoway calls the builtin `gdi natscale` (ado/base/t/tickset_g.class set_ticks), so dash can call it only where Stata runs, at export, which S45's stata_ticks table already does for every axis and by() panel a spec draws (the three axes are drawn exactly at build: test_stata_ticks.py::TestBuildTicksAreStatas::test_auto_misses). After a move the saved page and the served app run without Stata, and the range a move leaves is the minimum and maximum of whatever rows every widget then keeps (any slider position, any combination of widgets), so it cannot be enumerated at export; a grid of precomputed answers is not exact either, because natscale's answer changes at breakpoints in lo and hi that only the compiled routine knows. Precomputing the ranges of single-value dropdown selections (a by() request per filter variable) would cover only those moves and was not built. The refit was tried again on the whole fixture: of natscale's own answers, the end ticks are always the data's ends rounded to the step, or one step further out where the rounded tick lies inside the data (all 2,952 random ranges whose r(max) is a tick), and given natscale's step and count the lowest tick is round((lo+hi)/(2*step) - (count-1)/2) in 2,939 of them (the 13 others, 11 with a step of 5x10^k and 2 of 2x10^k, start one step higher, from a centre 0.35 to 0.5 above an integer); but a random-walk search over the cost model with eight and nine terms (separate weights for too few and too many ticks, a cost per step mantissa, a two-tick case that need not span the data) kept 261 of the 264 drawn axes (best 2,839 random ranges), and a rule extending each rounded end by thresholds on its uncovered share (0.26 of a step below N ticks, 0.43 at N, given natscale's own step) matched 259 and 2,786. trunk #2 and #3 (natscale r(n) 2, r(min) 0, r(delta) 20 over 5 to 23) are two ticks that leave 3 of the data above the top tick, as natscale's answer does in 3 of the fixture's 40 two-tick random answers (each with r(max) reported as the data's maximum and a step of 2x10^k); the model's rule that two ticks span the data excludes them, and the search that allowed them still kept 261 axes. Re-scoped 26oct2026 (WP-34, plot:PT-13): the residual of GAPS4 plot:PT-13.

- [x] Title: Under bokeh serve a session's dashboard is still drawn on the event loop
  - File Names and Line Numbers: dash_render.py the generated app's bokeh serve branch (`make_document(curdoc())` when `__name__ != '__main__'`), _DashBuildHandler; dash.sthlp the serving section
  - Description: The residual of BUGS.md "Served build on the event loop" (WP-32, H3): python app.py and dash serve build a session's document on a build thread in _DashBuildHandler.on_session_created, but `bokeh serve app.py` serves the script through Bokeh's own ScriptHandler, which runs the whole app script for each session inside Application.initialize_document, synchronously on the server's one loop, and gives a script app no session-creation hook.   - Suggested fix: find a hook bokeh serve awaits before a session (a directory form of the app with server_lifecycle.py's on_session_created, or a handler bokeh serve can be given), measured under bokeh 3.8 and 3.9; else make dash serve the supported path and say that bokeh serve draws on the loop.
  - Resolution: Fixed 19oct2026 (WP-32), as the entry's third option: dash serve and python app.py are the supported way to serve, and dash.sthlp says that under bokeh serve each session's dashboard is drawn on the loop and other readers wait (the serving section's list of what bokeh serve lacks, and the build paragraph). The build itself still runs on the loop there, because neither entry point bokeh serve offers has a hook it awaits before a session, measured 19oct2026 under bokeh 3.8.0 (Stata's Python) and 3.9.0: bokeh serve builds only a ScriptHandler, NotebookHandler or DirectoryHandler (bokeh.command.util.build_single_handler_application) and takes no handler of its own; a script app keeps Handler's no-op on_session_created and is run whole for each session in Application.initialize_document, synchronously on the loop; a directory app (main.py and server_lifecycle.py) under `bokeh serve <dir>` logged "RuntimeWarning: coroutine 'on_session_created' was never awaited" and never ran an async hook's body, because LifecycleHandler.on_session_created returns the hook's result from an async method and Application awaits only that, and a plain hook ran on MainThread, the loop. The other route (the script finding the running Application through curdoc().session_context and inserting a handler on the first session) relies on Bokeh's private attributes and still leaves the first session and every session's script run on the loop, so it was not taken. Pinned by test/test_served_build.py::TestBokehServeAwaitsNoHook::test_a_script_app_has_no_session_hook, ::test_a_directory_apps_async_hook_is_never_run (they fail the day Bokeh awaits a directory app's hook, when a directory form of the app can build off the loop) and ::test_the_help_names_dash_serve_as_the_supported_path.

- [x] Title: The data file embeds numbers as JSON text (about 0.5 GB per million values)
  - File Names and Line Numbers: dash_render.py _dash_write_stata_data, dash_parse.mata _dash_json_number17
  - Description: GAPS3.md G3, re-verified at 6370ca4: numbers embedded as JSON text (~0.5 GB per million values).
  - Suggested fix: a binary (base64 float64) column form read by both renderers and the served route
  - Resolution: Fixed 19oct2026 (WP-32), as the maintainer ruled (DECISIONS D39 item 1, which lifted D36's deferral). Measured first (19oct2026, the writer through a stand-in sfi, the saved loader): a million values -- ten variables of 100,000 observations, half doubles, half ints, 5% missing -- were 19.8 MB in the row layout, written in 0.41 s and loaded (parse and frame) in 0.43 s; one int variable of a million observations 16.6 MB, 0.72 s and 0.61 s. The title's 0.5 GB was not reproduced; the cost was about 20 bytes a value. _dash_write_stata_data now writes the column layout (dataFormat "dash-columns-1", _DASH_DATA_FORMAT): `columns` holds one entry a variable, a string variable the JSON list of its texts and any other its values as one base64 string of little-endian float64, or float32 where every value is exactly one (a byte, int or float variable always is), each missing value a NaN (_dash_pack_column); the extended missing letters stay in extendedMissing, so . and .a to .z round-trip exactly. The same million values are 8.0 MB (one int variable 5.3 MB), written in 0.05 s and loaded in 0.03 s (0.02 s). Both loaders read it through _dash_read_data_json, which decodes the columns (_dash_decode_columns: every named variable's column present, a string column a list of texts of numberOfRecords, a numeric one of a listed dtype and exactly numberOfRecords values, a NaN or infinity missing, anything else a ValueError as for a file that is not JSON), and _dash_columns_frame, which the saved loader (DashRenderer._load_data) and the served app's _load_spec_and_data call (both copied into the app); the old row layout is still read. The file is still the one 0600 file _dash_private_write writes; the served build's no-parse floor is three bytes a cell (an empty text), where it was six, and reads the column layout's count from numberOfRecords; the cell and byte limits are unchanged. The help's jsonio paragraph says so. Pinned by test/test_binary_data_file.py (TestTheWriterWritesColumns, TestTheReader::test_a_malformed_file_is_refused, TestBothLoaders::test_the_saved_loader_reads_both_layouts_alike, ::test_the_served_loader_reads_both_layouts_alike, ::test_extended_missing_reaches_both_loaders); flipped to the column layout: test/test_string_value_export.py TestTheWriter (seven tests), test/test_extended_missing.py::TestTheDataPath::test_writer_emits_codes, test/test_help_claims_2.cscript HC2-38, test/test_help_claims_5.cscript HC5-16; test/test_help_claims_4.cscript HC4-15 and test/test_qualifier_in_stata.cscript QS-05 read the columns. Closes GAPS3 G3 (WP-32, G3b).

- [x] Title: dash_setup installs by version, not by hash
  - File Names and Line Numbers: dash_setup.ado (_dash_setup_pip); dash_setup_lib.py pip_install_argv
  - Description: Residual of GAPS3 I3 (WP-31 section 59): dash_setup installs packaging, bokeh, numpy and pandas from the index by version range (pip install "bokeh>=3.8,<3.10"), never with --require-hashes; a hash-pinned install needs every transitive wheel's hash for each platform and Python, which only a maintained lock file can hold.
  - Suggested fix: ship a lock file of hashes per supported platform and Python, regenerated at each release, and install with --require-hashes from it (ratification item 1 of WP-31 section 59).
  - Resolution: Fixed 19oct2026 (WP-32), as the maintainer ruled (DECISIONS D39 item 1, which lifted D38's deferral). dash_requirements.txt (new, shipped in dash.pkg beside dash_setup_lib.py) pins every package dash_setup installs and each of their dependencies with == and the sha256 of every wheel of that release: 17 entries, 654 hashes, for Python 3.11 to 3.14 on macOS arm64 and x86_64, Linux x86_64 and aarch64 and Windows amd64 (bokeh 3.9.2, numpy 2.4.6 on 3.11 and 2.5.4 on 3.12-3.14, contourpy 1.3.3 and 1.4.0 likewise, pandas 3.0.6, packaging 26.3, tzdata only on Windows). It is written by scripts/make_requirements_lock.py (new), never by hand: the requirements are read from dash_setup.ado (min_bokeh, max_bokeh, min_numpy, min_pandas, _dash_pymin), each target is resolved by `pip install --dry-run --ignore-installed --only-binary=:all: --platform --python-version --report` (which installs nothing), each resolved package's dependency markers are evaluated for the target (pip evaluates them against the host), and every pinned release's wheel hashes are read from PyPI's JSON API; generated 19oct2026 with network access. Every install dash_setup runs -- a missing package (stata_pip, the --user retry too) and venv() (stata_venv) -- goes through dash_setup_lib.lock_install (new): read_lock checks the lock (each entry name==version, an optional marker of python_version, sys_platform and platform_machine only, and sha256 hashes; anything else refused), installed_dists asks the interpreter what it has (a child, INSTALLED_CODE), lock_lines picks the requirement's lines (unless the installed version is inside its window, so a reused venv's bokeh 3.10 is not downgraded; a locked version outside the window is refused, naming the generator) and each dependency's that is not installed, and pip_lock_argv runs `pip install ... --only-binary=:all: --require-hashes -r <those lines>`, written 0600 in a private folder removed afterwards; without a readable lock or package list nothing is installed. Measured: lock_install into a new Python 3.14 venv installed the 14 packages from the lock, hash-checked, and dash's packages imported (bokeh 3.9.2, numpy 2.5.4, pandas 3.0.6); with --require-hashes pip leaves an installed dependency it does not list and refuses one it would have to fetch. The help (dash_setup.sthlp's new "The hash-pinned lock" paragraph, how to regenerate it, and the hash-checked manual line; dash.sthlp's Dependencies) says so. Pinned by test/test_requirements_lock.py (TestTheCommittedLock::test_it_is_well_formed, ::test_it_is_generated_from_dash_setups_requirements, ::test_every_requirement_is_pinned_inside_its_window, TestDashSetupRequiresHashes::test_stata_pip_installs_from_the_lock, ::test_the_user_retry_requires_hashes_too, ::test_no_install_vector_is_unhashed, TestTheGenerator); no test reaches the network. Flipped to the lock's vectors: test/test_setup_pep668.py (TestStataEntryPoints, three tests; TestTheBokehWindow::test_the_venv_route_downgrades_nothing), test/test_help_claims_8.py::TestDashSetupHelpMatchesTheAdo::test_it_installs_only_what_is_missing, test/test_bokeh_window.py::TestTheWindowIsDeclaredOnce::test_every_declaration_names_the_window, test/test_setup_honesty.cscript HON-21, HON-22, HON-26, HON-27, test/test_program_coverage.cscript's PEP cases (through _pep_vec); test/setup_sandbox.py answers the installed-packages probe and writes the requirement file as REQ <package> (test/test_setup_sandbox.py::TestTheHashCheckedInstall). Follow-up, same day, as the maintainer ruled (the lock pins the tested versions): dash_setup.ado's window gains numpy's and pandas' ceilings (max_numpy 2.5, max_pandas 3.1, the minor after the newest the suites run under; the install spec, the manual pip line and venv() through dash_setup_lib.window_requirement, which, like bokeh_requirement, drops the ceiling for one already installed at or above it), and make_requirements_lock.py pins each of packaging, bokeh, numpy and pandas to the newest version test/requirements-dev.txt and requirements-stata.txt hold (tested_pins): the lock is bokeh 3.9.0, numpy 2.4.3, pandas 3.0.1 and packaging 26.3, 16 entries, its header naming them (# tested:). The 19oct2026 lock had pinned bokeh 3.9.2, numpy 2.5.4 and pandas 3.0.6, newer than any suite runs under. Pinned by test/test_requirements_lock.py::TestTheCommittedLock::test_it_pins_the_tested_versions, ::TestTheWindowRequirement, ::TestTheGenerator::test_the_tested_pins_are_the_newest_of_each_file, test/test_bokeh_window.py::TestTheWindowIsDeclaredOnce::test_every_tested_pin_lies_inside_dash_setups_windows; test/test_help_examples.py and .cscript hold the help's two changed pip lines (the hash-checked one had not been pinned). Residual: a platform or Python outside the lock has no wheel to match and pip stops; an installed numpy or pandas at or above its ceiling is not reported, as bokeh's is. Closes GAPS3 I3 (WP-32, I3).
