Section 30 held an unspanned box narrower than dash's; measured 18oct2026 (StataNow 19.5, s2color and stcolor, SVG): twoway sizes every box, spanned or not, to its text plus its text box style's margin (title("Hello world", box justification(left)), subtitle, note and caption start their text 0.6 units inside the box, s2color's `margin heading/subheading/body/small_body vsmall`), and span only centres the box on the graph instead of the plot region. Bokeh draws a Title's box round its text and padding, and dash gave no padding without margin(), so the box hugged the text.
  - Suggested fix: pad a framed text box by its text box style's margin.
  - Resolution: Fixed 18oct2026 (WP-32, D-30.c). _dash_textbox_margin_px (new) reads the text box style (tstyle(), else the scheme's `textboxstyle <option>`) and its `margin <name>` through the scheme's margin ladder, and _dash_textbox_style pads a framed box by it when margin() is not given, in both renderers. scripts/extract_scheme_truth.py carries the six directives (textboxstyle title, subtitle, caption; margin heading, body, small_body) into every dash-*.scheme and test/fixtures/scheme_truth.json. span still keeps the box centred on the plot region, documented in the help. Pinned by test/test_textbox_placement.py::TestBox::test_an_unspanned_box_is_its_text_and_margin, test/test_textbox_placement.py::TestBox::test_no_box_keeps_no_padding; fixture test/fixtures/scheme_truth.json.

- [x] Title: colorvar() on a line plot draws the whole line in its first point's level
  - File Names and Line Numbers: dash_render.py GlyphMapper.map_line, GlyphMapper.map_rline, GlyphMapper._colorvar_paint
  - Description: Maintainer ruling D39 (D-15f), 18oct2026. A Bokeh Line takes one colour, so section 15 drew a line, tsline, rline's bounds and connected's and rconnected's lines in the colour of the first finite row's level. Measured 18oct2026 (StataNow 19.5, s2color and stcolor, SVG; colordiscrete and continuous, connect(stairstep), connected): twoway draws one path a colour level through that level's points in plot order -- on x 1..6 with z 1 1 2 2 1 3 the paths x 1 2 5 and x 3 4, level 3's one point nothing -- and the rows missing z one path in the colormissing() colour, drawn first; it colours no segment between two levels.
  - Suggested fix: draw one line a level, each from its level's rows.
  - Resolution: Fixed 18oct2026 (WP-32, D-15f). GlyphMapper._colorvar_line_parts (new) builds the colour key through _apply_colorvar and splits the line's rows by GlyphMapper._colorvar_level_index (new, BokehJS's binning, vectorised) into one source a level -- the missing level first, then every level of the layer's colour rows, empty ones too, so the served redraw pairs them by position -- and GlyphMapper._colorvar_line_draw (new) draws each by connect() and cmissing() in its level's colour, in map_line (line, tsline, connected, rconnected) and map_rline (rline, tsrline). Each source carries the row ids, so the saved page's filter callback keeps a level's rows after a move; the served app redraws them. Pinned by test/test_colorvar_line_levels.py::TestOneLinePerLevel::test_the_measured_paths, test/test_colorvar_line_levels.py::TestOneLinePerLevel::test_missing_levels_are_one_grey_line, test/test_colorvar_line_levels.py::TestOneLinePerLevel::test_each_bound_is_one_line_a_level, test/test_colorvar_line_levels.py::TestAfterAMove::test_saved, test/test_colorvar_line_levels.py::TestAfterAMove::test_served.
- [x] Title: colorvar() on a line splits a continuous variable into the colour bar's 256 bins where twoway draws its key's few levels
  - File Names and Line Numbers: dash_render.py GlyphMapper._colorvar_line_parts, GlyphMapper._apply_colorvar (the continuous path), GlyphMapper.map_scatter, GlyphMapper.map_connected, GlyphMapper.map_rconnected
  - Description: Found by WP-32 after D-15f landed (BUGS.md "colorvar() on a line plot draws the whole line in its first point's level"): a continuous colorvar() (no colordiscrete, colorcuts() or colorlevels()) on a line was split by the colour bar's 256 palette bins, so `dash line y x, colorvar(z)' on x 1..101 with z = (_n-1)/100 drew 101 lines where twoway draws five. Measured 18oct2026 (StataNow 19.5, SVG of `twoway line y x, colorvar(z)', z a float: (_n-1)/100, (_n-1)*.73, 1000+(_n-1)*13, and price of auto): twoway's cuts are its colour key's labels (0 .2 .4 .6 .8 1; 0 20 40 60 80; 1,000 1,500 2,000 2,500; 0 5,000 10,000 15,000), a label below the variable's minimum dropped (price's 0) as colorcuts() drops one; its levels are the intervals (-inf, c0], (c0, c1], ..., (ck, +inf) in n + 1 colours of the rule (blue to red for the hue rule: 7, 6, 5 and 4 colours), the minimum on the first cut a level of one point that draws nothing; the key is one line sample a level.
  - Suggested fix: cut a line's continuous colorvar() at the key's ticks and draw it, and its key, in those levels.
  - Resolution: Fixed 18oct2026 (WP-32). _apply_colorvar takes stepped (from _colorvar_line_parts, and from map_scatter's colorvar_stepped for the markers of connected and rconnected): GlyphMapper._colorvar_stepped_mapper (new) takes the colour bar's ticks -- natscale #5, or zlabel()'s -- as the cuts, drops those below the domain's minimum, and gives the bar a LinearColorMapper of the n + 1 level colours (the rule's, colorlist()'s, or colpalette() sampled) whose equal bins fall on the cuts, closed above as twoway's are; _colorvar_line_parts splits the rows at the same cuts through _dash_colorvar_step_index (new, in the served copy), so the line, the markers and the key agree, in the saved page and the served app. A scatter's continuous key stays the 256-colour bar (DISCOVERY Q5). The colours are the rule's, within 1/255 a channel of twoway's (the six-level hue is 0xcc where twoway writes 0xcb, as _dash_colorrule_palette documents). Pinned by test/test_colorvar_line_levels.py::test_a_continuous_colorvar_is_split_at_twoways_levels and test/test_colorvar_line_levels.py::test_the_key_has_twoways_levels, which failed on the unfixed code (101 lines for the first case). zscale(log), which this left on the log bar's 256 bins: Fixed 18oct2026 (WP-32), measured first (StataNow 19.5, s2color, SVG of `twoway line y x, colorvar(z) zscale(log)' on x 1..101, z = _n, 10^((_n-1)/25), 1 + (_n-1)*.5 and .01*_n, and auto's price): twoway draws the key on a log axis but cuts the line at the same levels as without zscale(log) -- the key's natscale labels (20 .. 100; 2,000 .. 10,000; 10 .. 50; .2 .. 1; 5,000 .. 15,000), a label below the minimum dropped -- in n + 1 colours of the rule. _apply_colorvar's stepped path now takes the LogColorMapper too: GlyphMapper._colorvar_stepped_mapper keeps the bar a LogColorMapper on the domain, drawn in _DASH_LOG_STEP_BINS (1,024, in the served copy) equal log bins each in the colour of the level its centre falls in, and leaves the level colours in _colorvar_step_colours, which _colorvar_line_parts gives each level's line; the line's split is the cuts' own (_dash_colorvar_step_index), and connected's markers take the bar's mapper, within one bin of a cut. Pinned by test/test_colorvar_line_levels.py::test_zscale_log_keeps_twoways_levels (three measured cases, both modes) and test/test_colorvar_line_levels.py::test_zscale_log_key_is_stepped_on_a_log_bar, which failed on the unfixed code (101 lines a case).


- [x] Title: graphregion(margin()) stays at the pixels of the size the page was built at
  - File Names and Line Numbers: dash_render.py _dash_graph_margin, _dash_by_array_styles
  - Description: Maintainer ruling D39 (D-37.a), 18oct2026. _dash_graph_margin added the margin's change times min(fig.width, fig.height) to the figure's min_border_* once, at build, and a page resized to another width kept those pixels; _dash_by_array_styles inset a by() array by fixed px at dash's 4-inch reference (3.84 px a unit). twoway's margin is a share of the graph's smaller side at any size (WP-31 D11's measurement), and measured 18oct2026 (StataNow 19.5, stcolor, SVG) by(foreign, graphregion(margin(l+20 t+10))) insets the whole array by 20 and 10 units while graphregion(margin(l+20 t+10)) outside by() draws exactly the graph without it.
  - Suggested fix: re-derive the borders from the drawn size on a resize, and give the by() inset in a unit that scales with the graph.
  - Resolution: Fixed 18oct2026 (WP-32, D-37.a). _dash_graph_margin attaches one CustomJS (_DASH_GRAPH_MARGIN_JS, new) on the figure's outer_width and outer_height that replaces each changed side's added px with the change times min(W, H) / 100, keeping what other passes added to the border; _dash_by_array_styles writes the array's padding as a CSS percentage of the cell's width, the units times min(W, H) / W from xsize()/ysize() or the scheme's graphsize (_dash_short_side_share, new), so the inset scales with the page; both renderers. A graphregion(margin()) outside by() on a by() graph still draws nothing, as in twoway. Pinned by test/test_region_remainder.py::TestGraphMargin::test_a_resize_redraws_the_margin, test/test_by_array.py::TestArrayInset::test_graph_margin, test/test_by_array.py::TestArrayInset::test_the_inset_follows_the_graphs_ratio.
- [x] Title: The whole-dashboard export leaves open data tables blank
  - File Names and Line Numbers: dash_render.py _DASH_COMPOSITE_JS (dash_composite_layout, dash_composite_save), _dash_add_composites
  - Description: DECISIONS D39 (D-53d), 18oct2026: Save as SVG and Save dashboard on a top-level grid composed the grid's exported image, in which a DataTable (a DOM widget) is blank, and added the caption "Data tables are not included" when a table was open. The maintainer ruled that the export draws open data tables.
  - Suggested fix: draw each open table's titles and shown rows over its place in the grid's image, from its model values, in both renderers.
  - Resolution: Fixed 18oct2026 (WP-32, D-53d). The composite's arguments carry the ids of the grid's DataTables (table_ids, replacing toggle_ids); dash_composite_tables reads each shown table's box against the grid view's and its column titles and rows from its columns, source and view filter (as many rows as its height shows, in its view's order; a reader's sort is not kept), and dash_composite_layout draws it after the grid image -- a white box, bold titles, a rule and the rows, each cut to its column with "..." -- in the PNG and the SVG; the caption is gone. The code is _DASH_COMPOSITE_JS, which the served app copies by name. Pinned by test/test_export_composite.py::TestTheLayoutArithmetic::test_open_tables_are_drawn_over_the_grid, ::TestTheLayoutArithmetic::test_the_table_boxes_come_from_the_views, ::TestInChrome::test_an_open_table_is_drawn_in_the_composite.

- [x] Title: Printing a dashboard with tabs prints only the tab that is showing
  - File Names and Line Numbers: dash_render.py _DASH_PRINT_HOOK_JS, _dash_print_models
  - Description: DECISIONS D39 (D-53e), 18oct2026: printing fixed the page at 1000 px and printed what the screen showed, so with tabs() only the active tab's graphs reached the paper (the help said to print each tab in turn). The maintainer ruled that printing prints every tab, fitted to the paper.
  - Suggested fix: while the page prints, replace each Tabs by one image per tab, each on a page of its own and scaled to the page, in both renderers.
  - Resolution: Fixed 18oct2026 (WP-32, D-53e). The print hook (code _DASH_COMPOSITE_JS + _DASH_PRINT_HOOK_JS, args roots, tabs and tables, built by _dash_print_models at the three document_ready sites) on beforeprint shows each tab of every Tabs through its views (never through active, so no callback or server sees a tab change), lays it out at once, exports its grid and draws it with its open tables and the tab strip marked as Save dashboard draws it onto a canvas (class dash-print-tab, role img, named by the tab's title) styled width 100%, max-height 100vh, object-fit contain and break-before page; the canvases replace the hidden Tabs until afterprint removes them and shows it again. A tab that cannot be drawn leaves its Tabs printed as before. layout(bs) pages get the same hook. Pinned by test/test_export_composite.py::TestInChrome::test_print_draws_every_tab_on_a_page_of_its_own[auto], [bs], ::TestPrint::test_the_print_models.

- [x] Title: Variables named __dash* give r(110); dash's working columns can give r(900) at c(maxvar)
  - File Names and Line Numbers: dash.sthlp:211-243; Q11
  - Description: Drop-in audit of 19oct2026 (.ultraplan/review/DROPIN-AUDIT-19oct2026.md at commit f81cd31), package 11 (major): ids DT-19; confirmed; tracked: documented. Registered as GAPS4 DT-19 (WP-35, section 35-08, Fix).
  - Suggested fix: Use tempnames or a frame for working columns
  - Resolution: Fixed 27oct2026 (WP-35, DT-19). Each export names its Stata-made working columns -- qualifier, join-order, time-series and weight columns, and 33-07's split columns and label copies -- with a prefix no variable (nor, on a build, value-label set) of any frame it reads starts with, __dash or __dsh<k>_ (dash_parse.mata _dash_reserved_prefix, read by the Mata name writers through _dash_col_pfx and by the four generators as an argument); the four r(110) refusals are gone; the spec carries the prefix as _dash_prefix and both renderers read it (dash_render.py _dash_prefix_of, _dash_col_name_re), so the saved page and the served app draw a user variable named __dashq1 as data. When the data leave no room for the columns under c(maxvar), they are made in a temporary frame of the variables the export reads (_dash_maxvar_plan, _dash_frame_vars, _dash_frame_put; per frame on a build of several frames), and r(900) is given only when even those leave no room. Found while planning: a qualifier or weight naming e(sample) read no row, because the estimates were held first; a byte copy made before the hold (_dash_esample_copy, _dash_esample_sub) gives twoway's rows on both branches and in every frame. Every column the renderers make for themselves -- the row identity, the marker-label, jitter, colour-bin, alias, missing-code, display-text and table columns -- is formed from the same prefix (dash_render.py _DASH_RP; a spec of another prefix is rendered, saved and served, by a copy of the module run with that prefix, _dash_module_for, _dash_row_id), the saved page's filter reads the code prefix from its config (code_prefix) and the colorvar() relevel script reads each line's row key from Python, so a variable named __dash_row__ is drawn, hovered and filtered as data in both modes. Pinned by test/test_working_columns.py::TestTheRenderer::test_both_modes_draw_a_user_dash_column, test/test_working_columns.py::TestTheRendererNames::test_a_user_column_named_like_a_renderer_column, test/test_working_columns_js.py::test_the_missing_code_prefix_comes_from_config, test_wp35_truth.cscript Q3508-1, Q3508-2, Q3508-3. Closes GAPS4 DT-19 (WP-35, DT-19).

- [x] Title: dash and dash_setup refuse a Python that Stata found by itself (python_exec never set), and the remedy loops back to the same refusal
  - File Names and Line Numbers: fresh-HOME probe: c(python_exec) is empty while python query gives r(execpath)=/usr/local/bin/python3 and initialized=0; dash.ado:290-319; dash_setup.ado:96-107; dash_setup_lib.py:829-834

Per M8 nothing checks whether Python is there: dash.ado's _dash_require_python is an empty documented hook, _dash_require_deps runs its version probe as before and retries it with capture noisily, so a Python that cannot start is reported in Stata's own words, then by the new _dash_python_failed (dash's advice naming python set exec and dash_setup), with Stata's return code; its messages name the Python through the new Mata _dash_pyname() (c(python_exec), or with none set the Python Stata found, read from sys.executable); dash_setup.ado no longer stops on an empty c(python_exec), _dash_setup_pystart retries noisily and returns the found Python, and dash_setup_lib.py's _linked() falls back to sys.executable, so the pip line names the Python Stata runs; the certification harness no longer skips or exits for want of c(python_exec) (the gates of 128 cscripts and extract scripts and cert_svg.do removed) and scripts/stata_python_exec.sh reports the Python Stata runs; dash_setup.sthlp and dash.sthlp say what happens with nothing set; Stata-side, so both modes alike. - [x] Title: Named graphs with function layers are capped by c(macrolen): two n(10000) layers can be refused r(134), and the advice 'set maxvar' does not always help
  - File Names and Line Numbers: probe3 r(134) at 408,235 characters; dash.ado:11366-11377; dash.sthlp:3713-3714
  - Description: Drop-in audit of 19oct2026 (.ultraplan/review/DROPIN-AUDIT-19oct2026.md at commit f81cd31), package 2 (major): ids plat:PT-4; confirmed; tracked: n() refusal documented. Registered as GAPS4 plat:PT-4 (WP-36, section 36-03, Fix).
  - Suggested fix: Per A-7: the function points of a named graph go to a private file under dash's temp folder, keyed by graph name; fix the message and the help.
  - Resolution: Fixed 27oct2026 (WP-36, plat:PT-4). A named graph's function points are kept in a private file, fp-<hex of the name>.txt in the Stata session's folder c(tmpdir)dash-<uid>/points-<pid>/ (0700, the file 0600), not in $dash_fpts_<name>: the five Mata accessors _dash_fpts_path, _put, _get, _drop and _clear (dash_parse.mata) and the ado program _dash_fpts_open, which makes the folder and the file through dash_render.py's _dash_fpts_dir and _dash_tmp_write_text; _dash_register_graph no longer refuses points longer than c(macrolen), r(134), and the help no longer advises set maxvar. Measured at c(macrolen) 645,200: four 10,000-point layers (869,169 characters) were refused r(134) where twoway draws them, rc 0; both are rc 0 now and the spec carries all 40,000 points. The file outlives clear all, as the registry's globals do; replacing the graph, a KPI or image in its place and dash clear remove it, and the folder of an ended Stata session is swept (_dash_points_sweep, from _dash_fpts_dir and dash clear's _dash_tmp_clear). Both modes read the same spec. Pinned by test/test_function_points_file.py::TestOffTheMacro, test/test_function_points_file.py::TestClearAll::test_points_survive_clear_all, test/test_wp36_truth.cscript Q3603-1, Q3603-2, Q3603-3. - [x] Title: contour above 1,000 distinct points fits a seeded subsample on a 100x100 grid (every sandstone help example); a repeated node keeps the smallest z; a different polygon cutter
  - File Names and Line Numbers: dash.sthlp:565-592; dash_render.py:13992-14003
  - Description: Drop-in audit of 19oct2026 (.ultraplan/review/DROPIN-AUDIT-19oct2026.md at commit f81cd31), package 12 (major): ids TR-13, stat:PT-19, sil:SD-19; confirmed; tracked: documented; ROADMAP D4. Registered as GAPS4 TR-13 (WP-37, section 37-03, Fix).

On a full grid, or with interp(none), dash runs twoway__contour_gen at export in a frame of its own (_dash_contour_gen in dash.ado, after _dash_zero_obs_check and in the frame the data are written from, on every route), at twoway's cuts -- ccuts(), levels(), else the z axis's interior ticks, under by() the first panel's, as twoway cuts every panel -- once per by() panel and for the Total panel, and with outlines, alpattern() or sort once more with line for the boundary lines; its rows ride the spec as contour_grids (_dash_cg_take, _dash_fn_spec_tail) and both renderers draw them (map_contour, _contour_gen_fill, _contour_parts, _dash_contour_panel_spec), so every sandstone example draws twoway's own polygons with no approximation note; scattered data with another interp() keeps dash's own fit, its repeated-node rule and its cutter (the help says so).  After a filter move that leaves out a row of such a layer both modes draw dash's own fit of the kept rows with the stale cue, and Stata's polygons again with every row back (A-26; _FILTER_JS writes the build back by stata_n, above the cap too).  Pinned by test/test_contour_gen.py (TestTheRenderer, both modes; TestTheHandOver; TestTheSavedPage; TestTheChannel), test_mode_parity.py "TR-13: contour from Stata's polygons" (and per by() panel, and after a dropdown move), test_wp37_truth.cscript Q3703-1..6; fixture test/fixtures/contour_gen_truth.json. - [x] Title: Key-text textbox options are not drawn: box (silent), bcolor(), fcolor(), justification(), alignment(), margin(), linegap(), tstyle()
  - File Names and Line Numbers: _DASH_LEGEND_SUBOPTS (dash_render.py:53797-53803); probes L_box..L_ts
  - Description: Drop-in audit of 19oct2026 (.ultraplan/review/DROPIN-AUDIT-19oct2026.md at commit f81cd31), package 8 (major): ids LT-3; confirmed; tracked: generic dash.sthlp:1043-1049. Registered as GAPS4 LT-3 (WP-43, section 43-03, Fix).
  - Suggested fix: Draw them (M11: every P6-P10 item is drawn, none only named).
  - Resolution: Fixed 04nov2026 (WP-43, LT-3), by ruling D69. Measured first (scripts/extract_legend_box_truth.do, test/fixtures/legend_box_truth.json): twoway's legend(box) frames each key text at the text's extent, one text size high (the baseline 0.85 of it below the top), no margin by default, the line inside, in the scheme's text box fill and line (#d9e6eb and black under s2color, white and black under stcolor; box, box_st); bcolor(gs14) fills and lines the frames, fcolor() fills them, lcolor() and lwidth() line them, a dashed lpattern() draws no line (stroke-opacity 0), and without box they draw nothing (box_bcolor, box_fcolor, box_lcolor, box_lpattern, bcolor_only); margin(large) pads each text 8 units a side, with or without box, and the legend grows by it (margin_large, box_margin_large); alignment(top) and alignment(bottom) raise the text 0.151 of its size, baseline lowers it 0.150, middle is the default, and the frame stays (align_*, box_align_top); linegap(5) adds 5 units to the line pitch (linegap5); tstyle(heading) draws the texts in the heading style, size() winning (tstyle, tstyle_size); justification() moves no text, twoway's key text box being its text's width (just_right, just_center). Bokeh 3.8 and 3.9 draw each key text as a .bk-label DOM element, so _dash_legend_key_text draws these through the Legend's own InlineStyleSheet tagged dash_legend_keytext: padding for margin() (every marginstyle form, _dash_margin_sides), a relative move for alignment(), line-height for linegap(), and for box a .bk-label::before behind the text (its line boxes less their half-leading, the padding included; background, and an outline inside); tstyle() sets label_text_font_size and label_text_color. Every length is in em of the key text, so scale() and the width scale carry it; only numbers, fixed words and #rrggbb colours reach the CSS. Measured in headless Chrome in both modes and both Bokeh versions: each frame is its text's width within 0.01 px and one text size high, the baseline 0.868 of it below the top, the keys where they are without box; margin(large) pads 2.304 sizes; alignment(top) raises the text 0.151 sizes and leaves the frame; holes(1) cols(1) box and by()'s cell (which copies the legend's stylesheets) draw them. A frame narrower than the label's least width (Bokeh's label_width, 20 px at the 4-inch reference) is that wide. The toolbar's PNG leaves out the Legend's stylesheet, so the frames, margins and moves are not in it (as filed in BUGS.md "The toolbar's PNG of a legend title drops the legend's stylesheet: a title above a subtitle is in the subtitle's style and a boxed title is unframed"). Pinned by test/test_legend_box.py::TestKeyText (saved, served), ::TestKeyTextFixture, test/test_legend_box_browser.py::TestKeyTextInChrome (release tier), test_mode_parity.py "WP-43 LT-3" (with a move case) and test_wp43_truth.cscript Q4303-2, Q4303-3. Closes GAPS4 LT-3 (WP-43, LT-3).

- [ ] Title: title(..., angle() box) turns twoway's text inside its level box; dash keeps the title level
  - File Names and Line Numbers: dash_render.py _dash_textbox_style, _dash_figure_title; test/test_title_boxes.py::TestTitleSubopts::test_angle_with_box_stays_level

A Bokeh Label turns its box with its text (measured in headless Chrome: a side-panel Label at 45 degrees is a turned frame, its slot sized to the turned box), and a Title has no angle, so dash draws the title level in its box and names nothing.   - File Names and Line Numbers: dash.ado:9653 (_dash_plot's call to _dash_stray_quote_refusal, right after the UTF-8 check); dash_parse.mata:12526 (_dash_stray_quote_refusal); test/fixtures/quote_truth.json
  - Description: Residual of GAPS4 LT-24 (WP-43, section 43-05), measured 04nov2026 against twoway itself: twoway checks the plot types, their variables and qualifiers, by()'s variables, name() and the option names before it reaches a stray "' in option text, so `twoway scatter mpg weight, by(nosuch, title("'x"))` gives "variable nosuch not found", r(111), and `twoway scatter mpg weight, title("'x") nosuchopt(1)` gives "option nosuchopt() not allowed", r(198). dash refuses the stray first in every case, with the stray's rc and words (") required", r(100), for both). The rc and first line agree whenever the command has no other error (all 57 probes of quote_truth.json).

- [x] Title: Plot regions in one by() row can differ by 1 px in height; twoway draws them equal
  - File Names and Line Numbers: dash_render.py by() grid layout (WP-41 41-05, d536b03e: the rows follow the width scale); test/test_legend_span_browser.py _key_row
  - Description: Noticed 05nov2026 while fixing test_legend_span_browser's TestByColourKeyInAHole under Bokeh 3.8. Since d536b03e the by() grid's row heights follow the width scale and are fractional, so Bokeh's whole-pixel frames in one row can end 1 px apart in headless Chrome (Bokeh 3.8: the middle column of the key's row; Bokeh 3.9: a panel in row 1); at 1ce34b02, before it, the frames in a row were identical. twoway lays a by() row's plot regions out equal.
  - Suggested fix: round each by() row's height (and each column's width) to whole pixels once, in the grid's own sizes, so every panel in a row gets the same frame.
  - Resolution: Fixed 05nov2026 (WP-43). The cause: BokehJS floors each panel's laid-out height to whole px (UIElement._update_bbox, both versions), and the browser splits the grid's columns in 1/64 px, so under the one proportion _DASH_BY_FIT_JS gives every panel a row's heights straddled a whole px (headless Chrome, by(rep78) at 1400 px: columns 419.547, 419.547 and 419.562 px wide, panels 336.98, 336.98 and 337.00 px tall, floored to 336 and 337; Bokeh 3.9 the frames' feet at 337.23, 337.23 and 338.23 px, Bokeh 3.8 335.23, 336.23, 335.23 and 690.23, 691.23). Now _DASH_BY_FIT_JS holds every panel half a pixel past a whole px tall -- the n + 0.5 px nearest the height the fit wants, kept while the fit wants less than 0.75 px more or less -- so the floor is one value in every row, and under aspectratio() (WP-41 BY-18) each panel's own height likewise, from its laid-out width; the grid is at most 0.5 px a panel row taller or shorter than before (by(rep78) at 1400 px: 838.98 px, was 839.97). No new CustomJS. Headless Chrome (Bokeh 3.8 and 3.9, saved and served): every plot region in one by() row shares its top and foot, and every one in a column its left and right edges, to 0.01 px -- by(foreign, total) (2 x 2, a hole) at 1400, 1000, 768 and 528 px, by(rep78) (3 columns) with and without aspectratio(1) at 1400, 1000, 900 and 768 px; with every panel's proportion disturbed by 1%, the hook sets it once more and leaves it. Pinned by test/test_by_row_frames_browser.py::test_a_rows_plot_regions_are_equal (release tier); test/test_legend_span_browser.py's _key_row reads a row's frames as one value again, to 0.01 px.

- [x] Title: Legend key shapes of rcap, rcapsym, pccapsym, dropline, pcarrow, pcbarrow and rarea are wrong
  - File Names and Line Numbers: z_key_zoom.png, y_rk_stcolor.png, p101_key.png
  - Description: Drop-in audit of 19oct2026 (.ultraplan/review/DROPIN-AUDIT-19oct2026.md at commit f81cd31), package 8 (major): ids PIC-11; confirmed; tracked: untracked. Registered as GAPS4 PIC-11 (WP-43, section 43-04, Fix).
  - Suggested fix: Legend-only renderers in twoway's key shapes
  - Resolution: Fixed 04nov2026 (WP-43, PIC-11). Measured first (scripts/extract_legend_keys_truth.do, test/fixtures/legend_keys_truth.json sh_*, s2color): each key is a line symxsize() long (374.47 of 2880 units, 13 units); rcap caps each end with a stroke of its cap marker's size (44.05 units high, sh_rcap); rcapsym and pccapsym centre the layer's marker on each end, dropline on the right end (a circle r 26.35, sh_rcapsym, sh_pccapsym, sh_dropline); pcarrow draws two barbs back from its right end, 38.61 x +-21.03 units (43.97 long at 28.6 degrees), pcbarrow at both ends (sh_pcarrow, sh_pcbarrow); rarea a rect 374.47 x 99.99 units in the area's fill, its outline inside the edge (sh_rarea). BokehJS drew each of the layer's glyphs' own legend pictures over one another (the caps and end markers as markers at the box's centre at 0.4 of its size, the arrowhead's lines, the area's band). Now _dash_key_painter keys a layer of these types (its recast() target included) by _dash_key_shape: key proxies in 42-02's form (_dash_key_proxy) whose Scatter paints through _DASH_KEY_PAINT_JS in shape cap, shaft and ends, head or rect across the legend's key box, read at paint time; the line, fill and marker are the layer's own, the head's length, half-angle and barb the arrowhead's, and each proxy's visible is linked to every renderer of its layer, so by()'s click hides the whole series in every panel (42-02's _dash_key_for branch of _dash_by_panel_matches, unchanged: it compares the proxy glyphs, which match). One difference is drawn: an end marker is centred a marker's outer radius in from the box's end, inside it, where twoway centres it on the end, because BokehJS draws each key in its own canvas of the box's size. Headless Chrome (Bokeh 3.8 and 3.9, saved and served, no CSP violation): the shapes span the key box, rcap's ink is 0.44 text sizes high (twoway 44.05 of 99.99), rcapsym's and dropline's 0.527, pcarrow's 0.507, rarea's the box; an rcap layer a move empties loses its key. Help (dash.sthlp, the legend paragraph) says so. Then (05nov2026, WP-43, LT-21, batch 43.6) that difference is closed: twoway's end markers overhang the symxsize() box, the text still one key gap after the box (sh_rcapsym: the text at 1164.73 as rcap's, 59.9 after the line's end; sh_rcapsym_cols1: a marker key in the column centred on the line), so _dash_legend_key_boxes makes the legend's canvas the key box plus the marker, moves the shape's canvas so its box sits in its column and pulls its text back over the overhang, and the painter, told the box's share (kw), draws the shape in the box with each end marker centred on its end (no inset when the canvas has room); a Bokeh-drawn key in the wider canvas is clipped to its box. Headless Chrome (Bokeh 3.8 and 3.9, saved and served, no CSP violation): rcapsym's ink is 4.27 text sizes wide as twoway's 427.2 units, its text 0.34 text sizes after the right marker's edge as twoway's, and where rcap's text is from the line's left end. Pinned also by test/test_legend_keys.py::TestEndMarkersOnTheEnds and test/test_legend_keys_browser.py::test_end_markers_on_the_ends (release tier). Each shape's key after a move is pinned by test_mode_parity.py's MOVE_CORPUS ("<type> beside a scatter, its key in twoway's shape, dropdown to Foreign", the seven types), and a move emptying an rcap layer blanks its key in both modes in Chrome (test/test_legend_keys_browser.py::TestKeyShapesInChrome::test_emptied_rcap_draws_no_key, served through the app's own callback). Pinned by test/test_legend_keys.py::TestKeyShapes, ::TestTheShapeScript, test/test_legend_keys_browser.py::TestKeyShapesInChrome and ::test_by_click_hides_a_shaped_series (release tier), and test_wp43_truth.cscript Q4304-3 (live twoway's key shapes beside both modes). Closes GAPS4 PIC-11 (WP-43, PIC-11).

- [x] Title: title() whose text is an apostrophe and 90s inside double quotes is drawn where twoway gives r(100)
  - File Names and Line Numbers: dash.sthlp:1080-1091
  - Description: Drop-in audit of 19oct2026 (.ultraplan/review/DROPIN-AUDIT-19oct2026.md at commit f81cd31), package 8 (major): ids LT-24; confirmed; tracked: documented. Registered as GAPS4 LT-24 (WP-43, section 43-05, Fix).
  - Suggested fix: Refuse option text with an unbalanced quote with twoway's measured rc and words (r(100), r(109) or r(198) by form); quotes inside if qualifiers and compound-quoted text keep today's handling (P4-5).
  - Resolution: Fixed 04nov2026 (WP-43, LT-24), per the maintainer's ruling P4-5 (20oct2026), which replaces the 24sep2026 stored-as-typed rule for option text. Measured first (scripts/extract_quote_truth.do, test/fixtures/quote_truth.json, 57 probes): a "' met outside compound quotes inside an option's parentheses -- a stray -- makes twoway stop on what follows it. When its " closes a plain string twoway says "too many ')' or ']'", r(132), with ) right after the apostrophe, else "parentheses do not balance", r(198); otherwise the first character outside quotes after the apostrophe decides: a blank, tab, comma, =, { or } "type mismatch", r(109); ( or [ "too few ')' or ']'", r(132); ) or ] "too many ')' or ']'", r(132); none ") required", r(100) (41 probes, title("'90s", size(large)) among them, its comma inside the string the apostrophe reopens). The plan's rule (D-43-05.g: r(198) for a closing quote, r(109) for a blank, comma or =, else r(100)) is corrected to these measured sets. _dash_stray_quote_refusal (dash_parse.mata) reads the command by value and _dash_plot refuses with twoway's rc and words right after the UTF-8 check, before anything is stored or written; compound-quoted text and a "' in an if or in qualifier or a weight are kept as typed (P4-5), and the three rc 0 controls draw. One order differs and stays open: twoway checks the plot types, their variables and qualifiers, by()'s variables, name() and the option names before the stray and gives their error first (by(nosuch, title("'x")) r(111), title("'x") nosuchopt(1) r(198); measured 04nov2026), where dash gives the stray's; the help says so. The JSE-42..49 plain option-text cases of test_json_escaping.cscript flip to twoway's rc and words; the qualifier and compound cases stay. Help (dash.sthlp, the '90s sentences) corrected. Pinned by test_json_escaping.cscript Q4305-12 (every probe through dash: twoway's rc and first line, nothing stored after a refusal) and Q4305-13 (the qualifier and compound forms kept). Closes GAPS4 LT-24 (WP-43, LT-24).

- [x] Title: Documented: xtick and xmtick share one tick length; out-of-range reflines are clipped from the margin; string/hex formats drawn %9.0g, dates past the browser range, margin fixed at build
  - File Names and Line Numbers: dash_render.py _dash_fmt_dump, _DASH_FMT_JS, _dash_tick_union, _DASH_TICK_UNION_JS, _DASH_TICK_BLANK_JS; dash.sthlp, Differences from twoway items 18 (Reference lines outside the axis's range are not drawn) and 19 (The plot-region margin is fixed when the page is built), Axis options and Reference lines; test/fixtures/tick_style_truth.json ax15_*

  - Resolution: Documented 06nov2026 (WP-44, AX-15), by ruling D74 (maintainer, 06nov2026). Measured 06nov2026 (scripts/extract_tick_style_truth.do, test/fixtures/tick_style_truth.json ax15_*, and display probes in StataNow 19.5): xmtick(3000) beside xtick(2000 4000) draws 22.4-unit ticks where xtick()'s are 44.9; xline(5100) and yline(45), outside the scale, are drawn in the graph region's margin; ylabel(, format(%21x)) writes +1.4000000000000X+003 for 10 (the exponent in three hex digits: 65536 is +1.0000000000000X+010, 0 is +0.0000000000000X-3ff), format(%16H) 4024000000000000 (the double's bytes, high first; %8H the float's, 41200000), format(%12s) 10 20 30 40 (on 33.3333333 it writes 33.333333, not %9.0g's 33.33333), and format(%16h) is refused r(198) "invalid format, %16h", as dash refuses it. Fixed in 44-02 (commits 3b6ab3a and a6c0da1): the axis formats %21x, %-21x, %16H, %8H, %16L, %8L and %#s are written as twoway writes them (_dash_fmt_dump and its twin dash_fmt_dump in _DASH_FMT_JS; measured over zero, fractions, negatives, a subnormal and large numbers in tick_style_truth.json ax15_fmtl_*: %-21x and %-16H are %-21.14e and %-16.9e, %#s at any width is %10.0g; %10x and %12H are refused r(198) "invalid format, %10x" by twoway and by dash), and xtick() beside xmtick() or xmlabel() draws its positions as major ticks without a label and the minor ones at the minor length (ax15_ticklens_x/_y: 44.9 against 22.4 units), through a per-axis CustomJSTicker union (_DASH_TICK_UNION_JS), a label writer that blanks the tick-only positions (_DASH_TICK_BLANK_JS) and a grid ticker that keeps the gridlines at the labels; no layout-time CustomJS. The margin reference lines and the margin after a resize have no drawing route under D69 (an Arrow or Span in the figure is clipped to the frame, AnnotationView.needs_clip; a margin recomputed at each resize needs layout-time CustomJS), so by D74 dash draws every reference line within the plot region and fixes the margin when the page is built, and dash.sthlp documents them as Differences from twoway items 18 and 19, led to from Reference lines and Axis options.   - Resolution: Fixed 08nov2026 (WP-45, ST-10). A shipped name's translation stands at BASE's place on the ado-path: SchemeParser._resolve_path reads a scheme-NAME.scheme or NAME.scheme found in a directory before BASE (_before_base_path, admitted by _admit), as findfile's first hit, and dash's dash-NAME.scheme otherwise; BASE is the directory whose s/ holds Stata's scheme.class (_ado_base_index), so with no BASE on the path (a spec built without dash.ado) the translation stands as before, and a directory after BASE (the working directory) replaces nothing. A user file of a shipped name that includes that name reads the translation there (_include). Both modes. - [x] Title: xsize()/ysize() with units (10cm, 3in, 200pt) are ignored with a note that leaks 'None'
  - File Names and Line Numbers: region_options.sthlp:155-170; dash.ado:3753; float() at dash_render.py:27374, 27437, 27742
  - Description: Drop-in audit of 19oct2026 (.ultraplan/review/DROPIN-AUDIT-19oct2026.md at commit f81cd31), package 10 (major): ids GW-1; confirmed; tracked: untracked. Registered as GAPS4 GW-1 (WP-45, section 45-04, Fix).

  - Resolution: Fixed 08nov2026 (WP-45, GW-1). Measured (scripts/extract_figure_geometry_truth.do U_*): twoway reads xsize()/ysize() as a number with an optional in, pt or cm in lower case, a blank before the unit allowed -- 10cm and 10 cm draw 3.937 in, 3in and 3 in 3, 200pt 2.778, 2.54cm and 72pt 1 -- and refuses one outside 1 to 100 inches (0.5in, 300cm, 200, 0.5, ysize(0.5in), ysize(200)) r(198) in three lines, "graph xsize invalid;", "minimum xsize is 1 inch", "maximum xsize is 100 inches"; 10CM and abc are style names, noted, the scheme's size drawn, rc 0. dash.ado's graph rule is xsize=graphsize,1,100 ysize=graphsize,1,100 now: _dash_validate_value's graphsize kind reads the size, converts it to inches (1in = 72pt = 2.54cm) and passes the inch number on, so the renderer draws the box in both modes, and prints the three lines with r(198) outside the bounds (ysize(101) had dash's own sentence); any other text passes on unchanged. The note printed for a size that is not a number, such as xsize(abc), is still dash's and still ends 'using None instead.'; WP-49 section 49-02 (LT-25) gives it twoway's words. - [x] Title: Colour edges: navy*52 intensity rule, blank stylelist element refused in dash's words
  - File Names and Line Numbers: colour_grammar_truth opt_17; stylelist_truth R14; dash.sthlp:1316-1349
  - Description: Drop-in audit of 19oct2026 (.ultraplan/review/DROPIN-AUDIT-19oct2026.md at commit f81cd31), package 10 (major): ids ST-22; confirmed; tracked: documented. Registered as GAPS4 ST-22 (WP-45, section 45-05, Fix).
  - Suggested fix: Match the clamp; reword the refusal
  - Resolution: Fixed 08nov2026 (WP-45, ST-22). Measured first (scripts/extract_colour_edges_truth.do): Stata's darkening rounds a channel that lands at exactly a half (c * 2c) down, and so clamps to the smallest channel, for 60 values of c, all at most 127 -- navy's 26 among them, so mcolor(navy*52) is #010304 and navy*51 #010102 -- and up for every other c; no float model of the division reproduces the set, so GlyphMapper._HALF_CLAMP holds the measured one and GlyphMapper._blend_intensity (every colour*#, fintensity() and scheme intensity, saved and served) and the scheme extractor's _apply_intensity clamp on it. A used blank style-list element is refused with twoway's first line, which names the option's class path (option(s) marker(fillcolor(`')  linestyle(color(`'))) not allowed for mcolor(), the same on every plot type), from new Mata _dash_stylelist_blank_words, then dash's own hint, r(198); twoway accepts a blank element of pstyle(), mstyle(), clstyle(), astyle(), bstyle(), dstyle(), jitter() and connect() and answers mlabel(), base() and cmissing() otherwise, and dash keeps its own line there (stated in dash.sthlp's Style lists). The navy*52 exclusions of colour_grammar_truth.json and intensity_truth.json are gone. Pinned by test/test_colour_font_edges.py::TestIntensity::test_row, ::TestIntensity::test_the_half_rows, ::TestIntensity::test_the_old_grid, ::TestBlankElements::test_the_table_is_twoways, test/test_option_validation.cscript Q4505-2, test/test_wp45_truth.cscript Q4505-1; fixture test/fixtures/colour_edges_truth.json. Closes GAPS4 ST-22 (WP-45, ST-22).

- [x] Title: A range type (rbar, rspike, rcap, rcapsym) widens the x axis over rows where both bounds are missing; twoway leaves those rows out of the axis
  - File Names and Line Numbers: dash_render.py (the range-type axis rows)
  - Description: WP-34 34-07 (TR-4, 24oct2026), measured in both modes against twoway: each axis reads every variable over its own rows, so an x on a row with both bounds missing still sets the axis range (dash_render.py _dash_stata_tick_requests row rule, D-34-07.b).
  - Suggested fix: Leave a row with both bounds missing out of the x axis range and its ticks, as twoway does, in both modes.
  - Resolution: Fixed 07nov2026 (WP-44 WE, AX-19). Re-measured first (scripts/extract_axis_rows_truth.do, test/fixtures/axis_rows_truth.json ax19_*): the registration had twoway's rule reversed. twoway reads each variable of a layer over the layer's own rows, a row its partner misses included -- scatter y x with y missing past row 20 of 100 ticks x 0(20)100, scatter yy x2 with x2 missing past row 20 ticks y 0(20)100 -- for every type that draws its own variables (the range and pc types too) and for the x of lowess, fpfit and fpfitci; lfit, qfit, lpoly and the ci fits tick over the rows they fit, mband and mspline over their own curve. rbar, rspike, rcap and rcapsym already read their rows so; every other type left the row out of both axes. Re-scoped by the maintainer (D76). Each such layer now carries its rows hull (_dash_stamp_layer_rows, read by _dash_layer_extent and the saved page's axis plan, on the served app's own source a filter move rewrites), stamped only where a row holds one of the layer's variables and misses another, so every other page is unchanged; the export asks Stata over the same rows (_dash_stata_tick_requests, no complete-case part). Left open: a bar whose y is missing at an extreme x spans no half bar there (BUGS.md "A bar row whose y is missing joins the x scale without its half bar", S3). Pinned by test/test_axis_rows_p9.py::TestEachVariableOverItsOwnRows, ::TestAfterAMove, test/test_stata_ticks.py::TestTheCompleteCaseTokens, Q4403-13. Closes GAPS4 AX-19 (WP-44, AX-19).

Pinned by test/test_axis_rows_p9.py::TestOffsetBars, Q4404-6. Closes GAPS4 AX-20 (WP-44, AX-20).

- [x] Title: A legend of several rows and columns draws its column gap as its row gap: colgap() and the scheme's legend_col_gap are not drawn there
  - File Names and Line Numbers: dash_render.py _dash_apply_legend (the cols()/rows() step: legend.spacing is the column gap only when the legend is one row); test/fixtures/style_leaf_truth.json D_grid_gap
  - Description: Found 08nov2026 by the maintainer's follow-up to WP-45 section 45-03 (ST-17). twoway lays a 2 x 2 legend's columns colgap apart and keeps its rows where they are: the second column's key text sits 920.2 SVG units (720 an inch) right of the first under s2color (legend_col_gap large), 980.1 under colgap(huge) or a scheme's legend_col_gap huge and 780.1 under colgap(zero), the rows at y 2546.49 and 2686.46 in all three. BokehJS draws a Legend's keys in a CSS grid whose one gap is the spacing, so dash, which sets the spacing to the row gap on such a legend, drew every column gap as the row gap and colgap() changed nothing.
  - Suggested fix: Keep the spacing as the row gap and give the grid the column gap as its column-gap.
  - Resolution: Fixed 08nov2026 (WP-45, ST-17). A legend of more than one row and more than one column gets the column gap -- colgap() or the scheme's legend_col_gap, in 4-inch px times the width scale's factor -- as its .bk-grid column-gap through its own stylesheet tagged dash_legend_colgap (_dash_legend_colgap), the spacing staying the row gap; a one-row legend keeps the column gap as its spacing; both modes. Pinned by test/test_style_files_more.py::TestDirectiveFollowUps::test_grid_column_gap, test_wp45_truth.cscript Q4503-7; fixture test/fixtures/style_leaf_truth.json. Graded S3 (WP-45): fidelity -- every grid legend's columns 14 px closer than twoway's under s2color (5 px for 19), 22 px at colgap(huge).
